listings.title: Packaging Automation & Data Engineering Intern (Spring 2027 - January Start)
listings.desc:
Packaging Automation & Data Engineering Intern   
 Location: San Jose, California, United States  
 Employment type: Internship  
 Organization: Packaging / Engineering Operations   
 About Astera Labs   
 Astera Labs is a semiconductor company developing intelligent connectivity solutions for AI and cloud infrastructure. Our products depend on high-performance interconnects and advanced semiconductor packaging to move data reliably across compute, memory, and storage systems.   
 Role overview   
 As a Packaging Automation & Data Engineering Intern, you will be part of the packaging team developing Astera Labs’ portfolio of connectivity products for leading cloud service providers and server and networking OEMs. You will focus on software tools, scripting, data pipelines, and databases that improve engineering efficiency, data quality, traceability, and decision-making across package development and manufacturing.   
 You will work closely with packaging engineers and cross-functional teams to translate engineering workflows into reliable software solutions. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys coding, structuring engineering data, automating repetitive tasks, and building practical tools for real engineering problems. You will have opportunities to work with package design data, manufacturing and qualification information, supplier inputs, and engineering analysis results.   
 Responsibilities   
 Develop Python-based scripts and applications to automate packaging engineering workflows, data processing, file handling, report generation, and repetitive engineering tasks.   
 Collaborate with packaging engineers to understand manual workflows, identify automation opportunities, define requirements, and develop maintainable software solutions.   
 Build tools to extract, clean, transform, validate, and consolidate engineering data from sources such as Excel, CSV, TXT, HTML, PDF-derived datasets, and structured design or manufacturing files.   
 Design and maintain structured databases or data repositories for package, substrate, assembly, qualification, supplier, and manufacturing information, with attention to data integrity and traceability.   
 Develop scripts and utilities to compare package design information, BOMs, design rules, material properties, supplier capability data, and other engineering datasets.   
 Create automated checks and review tools that flag missing information, inconsistencies, out-of-spec conditions, or potential design and manufacturing risks.   
 Develop internal engineering applications or lightweight GUIs/web tools that allow engineers to run automation flows, review results, and provide user inputs efficiently.   
 Support data visualization and dashboard development for engineering metrics, NPI status, qualification results, supplier capability, manufacturing data, or other packaging-related information.   
 Integrate data from multiple sources and help establish reusable data pipelines, naming conventions, schemas, version control, and documentation practices.   
 Support automation involving package geometry or design data, including processing information from package drawings, layout exports, DXF files, netlists, or other structured engineering formats when applicable.   
 Apply software-engineering practices such as modular code design, error handling, logging, validation, testing, and source control to improve reliability and maintainability of engineering tools.

 Working towards a B.S., or M.S. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field.

 Entrepreneurial, open-minded behavior and a hands-on work ethic, with the ability to prioritize a dynamic list of multiple tasks.

 Required experience

 Working towards an M.S. or PhD in Electrical Engineering or a related field.
 Cumulative GPA of 3.3/4.0 or higher.
 Entrepreneurial, open-minded behavior and a hands-on work ethic, with the ability to prioritize a dynamic list of multiple tasks.
 Ability to work with minimal supervision and deliver solutions in a fast-paced environment.
 Strong time-management skills and strong written and verbal communication skills.

 Coursework in RF/microwave, communication systems and signal analysis, semiconductor manufacturing, or circuit design.
 Understanding of or coursework in signal and power integrity is a plus.
 Understanding of or coursework in semiconductor packaging is a plus.
 Scripting or software-development experience in Python, Visual Basic, or equivalent programming languages.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with careful attention to detail when working with geometry, models, data, and documentation.
 Ability to communicate clearly, collaborate across disciplines, and follow through on defined tasks.
 Preferred experience
 Experience with physical-design or layout tools such as AutoCAD, Cadence Allegro, Cadence APD/SiP, or comparable tools.
 Experience using 3D electromagnetic-simulation tools such as ANSYS Electronics Desktop, HFSS, HFSS 3D Layout, or SIwave.
 Knowledge of semiconductor multilayer flip-chip packages, including FCBGA or FCCSP.
 Experience with package substrate stackups, copper pillars, solder bumps, BGA balls, package-to-board transitions, or high-density interconnects.
 Familiarity with S-parameter extraction and validation, including ports, Touchstone models, passivity, causality, de-embedding, or mixed-mode analysis.
 Exposure to power-integrity concepts such as IR drop, DCIR, PDN impedance, decoupling, or current-density analysis.
 Experience with thermal modeling, mechanical analysis, coefficient-of-thermal-expansion effects, warpage, reliability, or package materials.
 Familiarity with design-for-manufacturing, supplier design rules, package assembly, reflow, underfill, or OSAT workflows.
 Experience using Python, MATLAB, Visual Basic, spreadsheets, or similar tools to automate analysis, process engineering data, or communicate results.
 Prior semiconductor, package-design, hardware, supplier, or manufacturing experience through coursework, research, projects, or an internship.
 What success looks like

 By the end of the internship, you have contributed useful results to a package-design, SI/PI, thermal/mechanical, DFM, tape-out, or manufacturing-readiness workstream and can clearly explain your approach, findings, and impact.
 Internship experience and compensation

listings.title: Performance Engineering Intern
listings.desc:
Performance Engineering Intern
 Astera Labs · San Jose, CA · Internship · On-site 
 About Astera Labs
 Astera Labs builds connectivity solutions that help power modern AI infrastructure. Our products connect processors, accelerators, memory, and networks in systems where throughput, latency, bandwidth, utilization, and power efficiency directly affect customer outcomes.
 The opportunity
 Join the Performance Engineering team and help measure, understand, and improve system performance across AI and data-center workloads. You’ll work with real platforms and representative workloads to build reproducible benchmarks, analyze results, investigate bottlenecks, and communicate what the data means.
 This internship is designed for someone who enjoys combining systems knowledge, experimentation, and data analysis: define a question, design a fair test, run it repeatedly, inspect the traces and metrics, form a hypothesis, and recommend the next engineering action. You’ll work with experienced engineers on a meaningful project involving CPUs, GPUs, memory, CXL, PCIe, Ethernet, NVMe, or related connectivity systems.
 What you’ll do
 Learn the platform architecture, workload, benchmark methodology, tools, and success criteria for your assigned project.
 Design and execute reproducible performance experiments across hardware configurations, software stacks, workloads, and operating conditions.
 Measure and analyze metrics such as throughput, latency, tail latency, IOPS, memory bandwidth, GPU utilization, power, CPU utilization, and system-level performance.
 Run or support benchmark suites and workloads such as MLPerf, CXL and memory benchmarks, FIO, MLC, SPEC, database or vector-database workloads, AI inference, and custom application tests.
 Explore the performance impact of variables such as GPU count, batch size, memory placement, NUMA configuration, read/write mix, interleaving mode, link topology, and workload size.
 Capture and analyze system traces, PCIe or GPU data flows, memory behavior, logs, counters, and other evidence to identify bottlenecks and performance regressions.
 Develop Python or shell scripts to automate test execution, collect results, extract metrics from logs, convert data to analysis-ready formats, and generate plots or reports.
 Compare results across configurations, reference systems, software versions, or competitor platforms while documenting assumptions and ensuring valid comparisons.
 Investigate unexpected results by reproducing the behavior, narrowing the variables, and working with system, hardware, software, validation, and product teams to identify root causes.
 Help build repeatable performance test plans and methodologies that can be applied to new GPUs, systems, workloads, or product generations.
 Create clear technical documentation that explains the setup, workload, metrics, results, limitations, and recommendations.
 Present your project, results, and key learnings at the end of the internship.
 What you bring
 Coursework, projects, research, or hands-on experience in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, data science, or a related field.
 Foundational understanding of computer architecture, operating systems, computer networks, memory systems, GPUs, storage, or distributed systems.
 Programming or scripting experience in Python, C/C++, Bash, or another language used for automation and data analysis.
 Comfort working in Linux and using command-line tools, configuration files, logs, and source control.
 Curiosity about why a system performs the way it does and a methodical approach to designing experiments and interpreting evidence.
 Ability to work with data, identify trends and anomalies, question assumptions, and communicate technical conclusions clearly.
 Ownership, persistence, and a collaborative mindset in an environment where performance questions often require iteration across multiple layers of the stack.
 Helpful experience
 Benchmarking, profiling, performance modeling, workload characterization, or system-level debugging.
 MLPerf, FIO, Intel Memory Latency Checker, Linux perf, Nsight, NCCL, SPEC, or related performance tools.
 CPU/GPU architecture, PCIe, CXL, Ethernet, RDMA, NUMA, memory bandwidth, storage, or interconnects.
 Throughput, latency, IOPS, bandwidth, QPS, p99 latency, utilization, power, or performance-per-watt analysis.
 Python data analysis and visualization with tools such as pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, or comparable libraries.
 Slurm or other distributed-compute environments, automated test infrastructure, or CI workflows.
 Experience presenting technical results through concise reports, dashboards, plots, or demonstrations.
 Internship experience and compensation
 This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges from $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.
 Equal opportunity
 Astera Labs is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees. We value diverse perspectives and consider qualified candidates without regard to legally protected characteristics.

listings.desc:
Physical Design Engineer Intern
 Astera Labs · San Jose, CA · Internship · On-site 
 About Astera Labs
 Astera Labs builds connectivity solutions that help power modern AI infrastructure. Our silicon teams develop complex digital products where power, performance, area, timing, physical implementation, and manufacturability must come together reliably.
 The opportunity
 Join the Physical Design team and gain hands-on experience taking a digital design from RTL handoff through physical implementation and signoff. You’ll learn how physical design methodology and flow infrastructure turn design intent into an efficient, manufacturable layout while helping improve repeatability, productivity, and design quality.
 This internship is designed for someone who enjoys both engineering fundamentals and practical problem-solving: running a flow, reading timing and QoR reports, investigating a broken stage, adjusting constraints or configuration, and measuring the effect of an iteration. You’ll work with experienced physical design, CAD, front-end, STA, EMIR, and physical-verification engineers on a meaningful project.
 What you’ll do
 Learn the physical design flow, development environment, project structure, tools, and methodology needed to contribute effectively.
 Run an assigned block through the RTL-to-signoff flow, including synthesis, floorplanning, power planning, placement, clock-tree synthesis, routing, optimization, timing closure, and signoff.
 Review physical design inputs such as RTL or netlists, SDC constraints, technology files, libraries, LEF/tech files, QRC data, and PDK-related inputs.
 Analyze timing, area, utilization, congestion, clock skew, insertion delay, transition, DRC, LVS, EMIR, and other quality-of-result reports.
 Help identify and resolve flow, implementation, timing, congestion, physical-verification, or infrastructure issues with guidance from experienced engineers.
 Support PPA exploration by running controlled experiments, comparing configurations, tracking results, and documenting the tradeoffs between power, performance, and area.
 Work with physical-design flow configuration, scripts, experiment definitions, reports, logs, and reproducible work areas.
 Contribute to CAD and flow infrastructure improvements such as report generation, run orchestration, validation checks, log mining, root-cause analysis, or handoff packaging.
 Use tools and flows such as Fusion, Innovus, PrimeTime, Calibre, Voltus, or related EDA environments under engineering guidance.
 Collaborate with front-end design, synthesis, STA, EMIR, physical verification, and other teams on inputs, handoffs, signoff criteria, and issue resolution.
 Participate in design reviews, code or flow reviews, technical discussions, issue tracking, documentation, and project planning.
 Deliver assigned physical-design work in a reproducible, well-documented state and present your project, results, and key learnings at the end of the internship.
 What you bring
 Coursework, projects, research, or hands-on experience in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, VLSI, or a related field.
 Foundational understanding of digital logic, RTL, CMOS/ASIC design, computer architecture, timing, or semiconductor manufacturing.
 Interest in the physical implementation of digital designs and how layout decisions affect power, performance, area, timing, congestion, and manufacturability.
 Experience with Linux, command-line tools, source control, or scripting through coursework, projects, research, or prior experience.
 A methodical approach to debugging: understand the inputs, reproduce the issue, inspect reports and logs, test a focused change, and evaluate the result.
 Ability to learn unfamiliar tools and technical concepts, ask focused questions, communicate progress and blockers, and follow through on commitments.
 Self-motivation, professionalism, ownership, and a collaborative mindset.
 Helpful experience
 ASIC physical design, synthesis, floorplanning, placement, CTS, routing, timing closure, physical verification, or EMIR.
 Static timing analysis, multi-mode/multi-corner concepts, clock constraints, setup/hold analysis, slack, skew, or useful skew.
 Power planning, standard-cell placement, macro placement, congestion analysis, DRC/LVS, antenna checks, or power-integrity analysis.
 Tcl, Python, Bash, YAML, or other scripting and configuration languages used to automate engineering workflows.
 Synopsys Fusion Compiler, Cadence Innovus, PrimeTime, Calibre, Voltus, or comparable EDA tools.
 Git, Bitbucket, P4, Slurm, Snakemake, or other tools used for reproducible, compute-intensive engineering flows.
 Experience comparing QoR across experiments, generating reports, visualizing trends, or debugging flow infrastructure.
 Internship experience and compensation
 This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges from $35/hour to $55/hour. listings.title: Product Engineering Intern
listings.desc:
Product Engineering Intern
 Location: San Jose, California
 Employment type: U.S. internship
 Work arrangement: Fully in-office
 About the role
 As a Product Engineering Intern, you will help support Astera Labs semiconductor products throughout the product lifecycle—from concept and engineering samples through characterization, qualification, production release, and continuous improvement. You will work alongside experienced product, test, hardware, validation, firmware/software, packaging, quality, and operations engineers to turn product requirements and test data into reliable, manufacturable products.
 This is a hands-on opportunity to apply your coursework to semiconductor product development, data-driven problem solving, and hardware/software systems. You will contribute to meaningful work with visible product impact, receive mentorship, and communicate your results to technical stakeholders.
 What you’ll do
 Learn Astera Labs products, architectures, datasheets, test requirements, and product-engineering processes.
 Support product development activities across characterization, qualification, engineering samples, manufacturing release, and post-release improvement.
 Review product requirements, datasheets, test plans, test coverage, characterization plans, qualification plans, and related engineering documentation.
 Help debug automated test equipment (ATE) failures through data analysis, bench correlation, and collaboration with test and hardware engineers.
 Analyze product-performance, yield, correlation, and test data across wafer sort, package test, burn-in, and other product-development stages.
 Assist with statistical analysis, test-limit setting, margin analysis, and the preparation of characterization, qualification, quality, and product-performance reports.
 Participate in board and test-hardware design reviews, including load boards, qualification boards, and other hardware used to evaluate semiconductor products.
 Help investigate low-yielding lots, test escapes, quality issues, and customer returns, and support root-cause and corrective-action activities.
 Work with design, design verification, design-for-test, hardware, firmware/software, packaging, OSAT, validation, test engineering, quality, product applications, and program-management teams.
 Prepare clear technical documentation, data summaries, and presentations that explain your approach, findings, impact, and learning.
 Present your intern project results and learnings to the team at the end of the internship.
 What you bring
 Current enrollment in a bachelor’s, master’s, or PhD program in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related technical field.
 Strong technical fundamentals and evidence of applying them through coursework, laboratory work, research, internships, co-ops, senior design, hackathons, or personal projects.
 Interest in semiconductor products, computer systems, digital or mixed-signal electronics, hardware/software systems, product testing, validation, or manufacturing.
 Ability to build, test, debug, analyze, and explain technical work—not simply list tools or technologies.
 Familiarity with at least one programming or scripting language, such as Python, C/C++, or MATLAB, through coursework or projects.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, attention to detail, curiosity, and willingness to learn quickly.
 Interest in working with data, automation, visualization, measurement results, or reproducible engineering workflows.

listings.title: Packaging Automation & Data Engineering Intern
listings.desc:
Packaging Automation & Data Engineering Intern   
 Location: San Jose, California, United States  
 Employment type: Internship  
 Organization: Packaging / Engineering Operations   
 About Astera Labs   
 Astera Labs is a semiconductor company developing intelligent connectivity solutions for AI and cloud infrastructure. Our products depend on high-performance interconnects and advanced semiconductor packaging to move data reliably across compute, memory, and storage systems.   
 Role overview   
 As a Packaging Automation & Data Engineering Intern, you will be part of the packaging team developing Astera Labs’ portfolio of connectivity products for leading cloud service providers and server and networking OEMs. You will focus on software tools, scripting, data pipelines, and databases that improve engineering efficiency, data quality, traceability, and decision-making across package development and manufacturing.   
 You will work closely with packaging engineers and cross-functional teams to translate engineering workflows into reliable software solutions. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys coding, structuring engineering data, automating repetitive tasks, and building practical tools for real engineering problems. You will have opportunities to work with package design data, manufacturing and qualification information, supplier inputs, and engineering analysis results.   
 Responsibilities   
 Develop Python-based scripts and applications to automate packaging engineering workflows, data processing, file handling, report generation, and repetitive engineering tasks.   
 Collaborate with packaging engineers to understand manual workflows, identify automation opportunities, define requirements, and develop maintainable software solutions.   
 Build tools to extract, clean, transform, validate, and consolidate engineering data from sources such as Excel, CSV, TXT, HTML, PDF-derived datasets, and structured design or manufacturing files.   
 Design and maintain structured databases or data repositories for package, substrate, assembly, qualification, supplier, and manufacturing information, with attention to data integrity and traceability.   
 Develop scripts and utilities to compare package design information, BOMs, design rules, material properties, supplier capability data, and other engineering datasets.   
 Create automated checks and review tools that flag missing information, inconsistencies, out-of-spec conditions, or potential design and manufacturing risks.   
 Develop internal engineering applications or lightweight GUIs/web tools that allow engineers to run automation flows, review results, and provide user inputs efficiently.   
 Support data visualization and dashboard development for engineering metrics, NPI status, qualification results, supplier capability, manufacturing data, or other packaging-related information.   
 Integrate data from multiple sources and help establish reusable data pipelines, naming conventions, schemas, version control, and documentation practices.   
 Support automation involving package geometry or design data, including processing information from package drawings, layout exports, DXF files, netlists, or other structured engineering formats when applicable.   
 Apply software-engineering practices such as modular code design, error handling, logging, validation, testing, and source control to improve reliability and maintainability of engineering tools.   
 Help improve existing scripts and engineering tools by debugging issues, optimizing performance, refactoring code, and adding new capabilities based on user feedback.   
 Prepare clear documentation for scripts, databases, data structures, workflows, assumptions, and user instructions so solutions can be maintained and reused by the team.   
 Support communication with internal engineering teams, substrate suppliers, and OSAT partners when data collection, standardization, or automation interfaces are required.   
 Present completed projects, technical approach, results, and measurable efficiency or quality improvements at the end of the internship.   
 Basic qualifications   
 Working towards a B.S., or M.S. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field.   
 Cumulative GPA of 3.2/4.0 or higher.   
 Entrepreneurial, open-minded behavior and a hands-on work ethic, with the ability to prioritize a dynamic list of multiple tasks.   
 Ability to work with minimal supervision and deliver solutions in a fast-paced environment.   
 Strong time-management skills and strong written and verbal communication skills.   
 Required experience   
 Coursework or project experience in programming, data structures, databases, software engineering, data analytics, or engineering computation.   
 Strong programming experience in Python; experience with common data-processing libraries such as pandas, NumPy, or equivalent tools.   
 Experience working with structured data and databases, including SQL and relational database concepts.   
 Experience developing scripts or software for automation, data processing, file parsing, analysis, or engineering applications.   
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with careful attention to data quality, edge cases, validation, and reproducibility.   
 Ability to communicate clearly, collaborate with engineers from different disciplines, and translate engineering requirements into practical software solutions.   
 Preferred experience   
 Experience with Python GUI or web-application frameworks such as PyQt/PySide, Streamlit, Flask, FastAPI, or comparable tools.   
 Experience with SQL databases such as SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, or similar platforms, including schema design, queries, and data integration.   
 Experience with Git or other version-control systems and familiarity with collaborative software-development practices.   
 Experience with data visualization or dashboard tools such as Plotly, Power BI, Tableau, Matplotlib, or similar tools.   
 Experience parsing or generating engineering file formats and automating Microsoft Excel or other office workflows using Python, APIs, or similar methods.   
 Familiarity with APIs, ETL/data pipelines, REST services, cloud databases, or data-management platforms is a plus.   
 Exposure to machine learning, computer vision, large-language-model applications, or AI-assisted engineering workflows is a plus.   
 Understanding of semiconductor packaging, electronics manufacturing, package design, FCBGA/FCCSP, substrate technology, or OSAT workflows is a plus but not required.   
 Experience developing software or automation for engineering, laboratory, manufacturing, research, or hardware-related applications.   
 Prior internship, research, coursework, or personal projects demonstrating ownership of a software, database, automation, or data-analysis project from problem definition through implementation.   
 What success looks like   
 You learn the packaging team’s engineering workflows and data environment, then take ownership of one or more automation or data-engineering projects with appropriate guidance.   
 You deliver reliable, documented, and reusable code or database solutions that reduce manual work, improve data quality, or make engineering information easier to access and analyze.   
 By the end of the internship, you have deployed or demonstrated useful tools for scripting, data processing, database management, engineering review automation, or visualization and can clearly explain the problem, architecture, implementation, validation, and impact.   
 Internship experience and compensation   
 This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges from $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipen

listings.title: Controls Application Engineering Intern -1
listings.desc:
Job Description Summary 
The Control Application Engineer Intern will work in the Control and Protections Systems Department within the HVDC unit of GE Vernova to support the design and implementation of HVDC Control and Protection Systems to meet the demands of the grid and renewable energy market. As leaders in the energy space our goal is to accelerate the transition for a more energy efficient grid to fulfil the needs of tomorrow. Our projects are unique and interesting, and you’ll need to bring a solution-focused, positive approach to each one to do your best to collaborate with world renowned experts on game-changing technologies. 
 Job Description 
 About us:
 UK Grid Solutions Limited - Power Electronics, Stafford is an international leader in high power electronics and control technology, specialising in the engineering of High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) Transmission Systems using both Line-Commutated (thyristor-based) and Voltage-Sourced (IGBT-based) converter technologies.
 With over 50 years of experience in HVDC, GE worldwide HVDC Centre of Excellence in Stafford provides complete turn-key solutions for the rapidly-growing global HVDC market. Project Management, Engineering, Manufacturing, Test Laboratories and Research & Development are all located in Stafford. This unique setup gives HVDC engineers at Stafford exposure across the manufacturing cycle; allowing innovation and design to quickly influence new and existing products. The HVDC Technology Departments are at the forefront of worldwide innovation in HVDC and are expanding rapidly. 
 Role overview:
 As an Intern you will report within the Control and Protections Systems Department. The successful candidate will be part of a highly motivated, dynamic and growing team of engineers working on the design of HVDC Control Systems. This is a very exciting and dynamic field of control engineering in which GE’s leading contribution has worldwide recognition. 
 HVDC Control & Protection Systems Engineering supports the design and implementation of HVDC Control and Protection Systems by analysing customer requirements, assessing the necessary deviation from standard solutions, modelling the proposed HVDC control system, providing requirements for the hardware and software teams to implement and validate the resulting system.
 Responsibilities:
 • Work as part of an expert team, giving ample opportunity for learning design and development skills highly relevant for working with any control and protection system; in particular, power electronics systems and grid technology.
 • Execute with guidance from senior engineering resources, the analysis, simulation, test, and integration required to define, and support assigned components, modules or systems that meet business standards Including: 
 • PSSE/PSCAD and PSSE/RSCAD Power system network conversion, modelling and verification.
 • Plant modelling of HVDC System in various simulation tools (MATLAB, RSCAD, PSCAD etc) and its verification. 
 • Support in producing required technical documentation, under the supervision of senior engineers.
 • Follow the departments standard design practices, engineering reviews and guidelines.
 • Use some level of judgment and has ability to propose different solutions outside of set parameters but with guidance
 The Person:
 The candidate will have completed 2 years of degree level in a related science such as Electrical Engineering, or equivalent knowledge or experience. 
 However, this is not as important as a proven track record and evidence that you have the mind-set and abilities to perform the role.
 Needs to be eligible to work in the UK. No Visa support will be provided.

listings.desc:
About GlobalFoundries  
 GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling AI at scale from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GF delivers differentiated, power-efficient and high-performance solutions for high-growth markets. GF is a trusted and holistic technology partner for customers around the world. GF’s talented, global team remains focused every day on security, longevity and sustainability. For more information, visit www.gf.com . 
 Internship Program Overview:  
 Our Interns & Co-ops are our entry-level talent pipeline for GF across the globe. Our goal is to provide students with a meaningful work experience that will equip them with the skills to embark on a career in the fast-paced and growing semiconductor industry after graduation. As an intern at GF, you’ll experience one-on-one mentorship, work assignments that prioritize your growth and potential, professional development opportunities, and the chance to network with executives. 
 Summary of Role:  
 The Software Engineering Intern will contribute to an innovative software performance-tuning application for MIPS RISC-V microprocessors. This role provides hands-on experience with application development, simulation and modeling concepts, developer tools, performance analysis, testing, and customer-focused software workflows. 
 Essential Responsibilities include:  
 Contribute to well-scoped software features, prototypes, tests, automation, and tooling improvements under the guidance of experienced engineers. 
 Learn how the application supports software performance tuning for MIPS RISC-V microprocessors, including front-end workflows, back-end simulation concepts, and data visualization. 
 Assist with debugging, testing, documentation, and enhancements that improve product quality, usability, and developer productivity. 
 Participate in code reviews, design discussions, team meetings, and technical demonstrations, and present project progress and outcomes to mentors and team members. 
 Other Responsibilities:  
 Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs. 
 Required Qualifications:  
 Education – At least a sophomore at time of application and actively pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, or related field through an accredited degree program during the time of internship. 
 Must have at least an overall 3.0 GPA and be in good academic standing. 
 Language Fluency - English (Written & Verbal) 
 Ability to work at least 40 hours per week during the internship. 
 Preferred Qualifications:  
 Prior related internship or co-op experience 
 Demonstrated prior leadership experience in the workplace, school projects, competitions, etc. 
 Strong interest in leveraging AI tools and emerging technologies to enhance productivity, streamline workflows, and support effective decision-making. 
 Project management skills, i.e., the ability to innovate and execute on solutions that matter; the ability to navigate ambiguity. 
 Strong written and verbal communication skills 
 Strong planning & organizational skills 
 Strong programming fundamentals developed through coursework, labs, personal projects, open-source contributions, internships, or research. 
 Interest in developer tools, application frameworks, data visualization, computer architecture, RISC-V, simulation, performance tuning, compilers, operating systems, or low-level software systems.

listings.location: Austin, TX; Santa Clara, CA; Hillsboro, OR; Folsom, CA; Phoenix, AZ

Job Details: 
 Job Description: 
 What if your next project helped power the future of technology? 
 At Intel, you'll do more than learn, you'll contribute. You'll work side-by-side with industry leaders, gain hands-on experience on meaningful projects, and help solve real-world challenges that affect billions of people worldwide. From advanced semiconductor manufacturing to AI-powered innovations, you'll play a role in technologies that redefine how the world works, learns, and connects.
 What makes Intel unique is the opportunity to see the entire technology lifecycle in action. Unlike many companies where hardware, software, and manufacturing operate separately, Intel brings them together, giving you exposure to everything from research and design to advanced semiconductor manufacturing and global deployment.
 Whether you're tackling engineering challenges, improving operations, analyzing data, advancing next-generation technologies, or supporting global customers, you'll build valuable skills while contributing to innovations that enable a more sustainable and connected future.
 Bring your curiosity, make an impact, and see where your ideas can take you at Intel. 
 What You'll Do 
 Build technologies that power the future of computing. As a Platform Hardware and Systems Engineering Intern, you'll work on meaningful projects while building technical expertise that accelerates your professional growth.
 Hardware and systems architecture, design, and integration.
 Platform validation, debug, and performance optimization.
 Power, thermal, and signal integrity engineering.
 Programming, automation, and AI-enabled solutions.
 Cross-functional work that advances platform capabilities.
 Develop technical depth, tackle complex challenges, and contribute from day one while learning alongside experienced Intel engineers and technical leaders.
 Where Your Career Could Take You 
 Potential opportunity areas include:
 Hardware Design Engineer
 Systems Engineering & Architecture roles
 Platform Validation Engineer
 Power & Signal Integrity Engineer
 GPU Platform Hardware Design Engineer
 Silicon & Packaging Engineer
 Emerging Technologies & Research roles
 Build technical expertise, explore new possibilities, and help shape what is next in computing and semiconductor technology.
 Qualifications: 
 Must possess the minimum qualifications below to be initially considered for this position. Experience may be gained through coursework, research, academic projects, internships, laboratory work, student organizations, leadership experiences, or other relevant experiences.
 Minimum Qualifications 
 Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, Chemistry, Mathematics, Physics, or a related STEM field.
 3+ months of experience gained through coursework, academic projects, research, internships, co-ops, student organizations, assistantships, or other relevant technical experiences.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 GPA of 3.0 or higher preferred.
 Experience or interest in design, architecture, programming, scripting, data analysis, automation, modeling, simulation, validation, or debugging.
 Hands-on coursework, research, projects, or internship experience related to the role family.
 Strong problem-solving, communication, collaboration, and ability to work in team-based environments.
 Location & Immigration Information 
 As you consider the opportunity to join Intel, relocation assistance may be available based on eligibility, current location, and the specifics of the role.
 Job location and modality of work will be communicated at time of offer. This position is not available in the state of Colorado. 
 This position is not eligible for employment-based visa/immigration sponsorship. 
 Intel sponsors individuals for employment-based visas for positions where we experience a shortage of U.S. workers. These skills shortage roles are typically STEM positions requiring a Master's or PhD degree, or a Bachelor's degree with at least three years of post-degree related job experience. This position does not qualify for Intel sponsorship because it is either a non-STEM position, or a STEM position that only requires a Bachelor's degree and less than three years' experience.
 For information on Intel's immigration sponsorship guidelines, please see: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/jobs/hiring.html

 Strong written and verbal communication skills

listings.desc:
NXP Global Sales Introduction 
 AI is rapidly moving beyond research labs and into the real world—powering advancements in vehicles, factories, hospitals, homes, and connected devices. NXP brings together secure edge intelligence, advanced semiconductor solutions, and deep system expertise to help customers build what’s next. Our Global Sales and Applications organization partners with customers to align technical solutions to application requirements, solve integration challenges, and accelerate design wins. We are seeking a technically curious engineering student to join our Field Applications team and help enable the integration of NXP semiconductor technologies into real customer systems.
 Program Overview 
 The NXP Americas Global Sales & Applications Summer Internship is a 12 week, paid program for rising juniors, seniors, and graduate students who combine a strong technical foundation with the drive and curiosity to work directly with customers. Interns are embedded in the Field Application Engineering organization, paired with an experienced FAE mentor, and assigned meaningful technical work from day one.
 This internship is a primary pipeline into NXP’s Technical Sales & Applications Program (TSAP), our early-career pathway for full-time technical sales and applications roles. Strong performers may receive a return offer upon graduation.
 What You'll Do 
 As a Field Applications Engineering Intern, you will work alongside experienced FAEs on customer-facing technical projects with real business impact. You will help translate application requirements into practical NXP-based solutions, support evaluations and proof-of-concepts, and develop hands-on experience with embedded systems, lab validation, and design-in activity. Sample responsibilities include:
 Customer Application Support 
 Work alongside FAEs to understand customer requirements and help select appropriate NXP MCUs, MPUs, connectivity, analog, power-management, and edge-processing solutions. 
 Support technical customer meetings, design reviews, product evaluations, proof-of-concept activities, and NXP solution demonstrations. 
 Help analyze customer issues, reproduce problems, document findings, and contribute to clear technical action plans and follow-up. 
 Embedded Development & System Integration 
 Bring up evaluation boards and reference designs; configure SDKs and development environments; and integrate example software into application prototypes. 
 Develop or modify firmware and application code in C, C++, Python, or similar languages under the guidance of experienced engineers. 
 Support embedded software debugging and system integration across real-time control, sensor interfaces, connectivity, Linux, or RTOS-based applications. 
 Lab Validation & Design Support 
 Perform product evaluation, lab validation, and basic system-level troubleshooting using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multimeters, power supplies, current/voltage probes, power analyzers, and software debug or trace tools. 
 Assist with schematic and PCB reviews, interface checks, power-up sequencing, signal observations, and hardware/software integration investigations. 
 Create concise test plans, capture measurements, organize results, and communicate conclusions to technical and non-technical stakeholders. 
 Technical Enablement & Communication 
 Prepare customer-ready technical presentations, demonstrations, quick-start guides, application notes, and training material with guidance from senior engineers. 
 Capture customer feedback and collaborate with sales, marketing, product management, product-line, and engineering teams to improve tools, software, documentation, and support content. 
 Present your summer project findings, technical approach, results, and recommendations to sales and applications leadership in a final intern capstone presentation. 
 About You 
 Minimum Qualifications 
 Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Mechatronics, or a related technical field. 
 Rising junior, senior, or graduate student — expected graduation between December 2027 and June 2029. 
 Cumulative GPA of 3.0/4.0 or higher. 
 Authorization to work in the United States (no sponsorship available for intern roles). 
 Availability for 12 weeks full-time during Summer 2027 (May–August). 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Coursework or project experience in embedded systems, analog and digital circuits, computer architecture, microcontrollers/processors, wireless communications, power electronics, control systems, or semiconductor applications. 
 Hands-on experience with microcontrollers, MPUs, FPGAs, development boards, evaluation kits, or reference designs; familiarity with ARM-based systems is a plus. 
 Programming experience in C, C++, Python, or similar languages, with exposure to IDEs, SDKs, version control, RTOS basics, or embedded Linux. 
 Familiarity with common embedded interfaces such as UART, SPI, I2C, CAN, USB, or Ethernet. 
 Experience using or willingness to learn common lab equipment, schematic/PCB review, board bring-up, firmware debugging, sensor integration, motor control, edge AI, or robotics applications. 
 Who Thrives Here 
 You are curious about how semiconductor products solve real-world system problems and enjoy learning by building and testing. 
 You approach debugging methodically: form a hypothesis, measure the system, isolate variables, and document the result. 
 You communicate clearly with engineers, customers, sales teams, and non-technical stakeholders. 
 You are proactive, take ownership, collaborate well, and adapt to changing priorities in a customer-focused environment. 
 You are motivated to develop both technical expertise and business understanding while contributing to team results. 
 What You'll Get 
 Competitive paid hourly compensation. 
 Dedicated FAE/TSE mentor and day-to-day manager support throughout the program. 
 Hands-on exposure to the semiconductor applications cycle—from requirements discovery and technical evaluation through proof-of-concept and design-in support. 
 Participation in intern cohort events, including professional development workshops, executive speaker sessions, and cross-functional networking opportunities. 
 Access to structured learning on NXP product portfolios, embedded systems, customer applications, and the semiconductor industry. 
 Potential relocation support or housing stipend (location-dependent). 
 Consideration for a return full-time offer into NXP's TSAP program upon graduation. 
 Locations 
 Field Sales Offices across the United States — including but not limited to: Austin, TX | Detroit, MI | San Jose, CA
 Preferred location will be discussed during the interview process. Some local customer travel may be expected.
 How to Apply 
 Submit your application through NXP's careers portal at nxp.com/careers.

listings.title: Data Engineering Intern - AI & Analytics (January - August 2027)
listings.desc:
ABOUT US

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.



The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.



This is a general application used to fill multiple internship openings across our AI, Data, and Analytics teams. If selected, you will be matched to a specific team based on your background and interests during the interview process.

 - Data Engineering Intern - AI & Analytics

 - Data Engineering Intern - AI/ML

 - Data Engineering Intern - Analytics

 - Software Engineering Intern - AI & Machine Learning

 - Software Engineering Intern - AI Platform

 - Software Engineering Intern - DevOps

 - Software Engineering Intern - Execution Apps

 - Software Engineering Intern - Fleet Applications

 - Software Engineering Intern - Vehicle and Fleet Apps

 - Systems Analytics Engineering Intern - Connectivity and Telematics


ROLE SUMMARY

Software-defined vehicles generate enormous amounts of data, from vehicle telemetry to manufacturing and fleet operations. As a Data Engineering intern, you will help turn that data into usable, reliable infrastructure and analytics, working on data pipelines, machine learning platforms, or the software and analytics supporting fleet and manufacturing applications.

Specific project areas vary by team and may include:

 - Developing SQL and Python based data transformation and pipeline code

 - Building and maintaining ELT pipelines and analytics workflows on Databricks or similar platforms

 - Supporting machine learning model development, evaluation, or deployment infrastructure

 - Contributing to software for fleet management or manufacturing execution applications that depend on reliable data

 - Building automated data quality tests and integrating with CI/CD workflows


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design, build, or maintain data pipelines, analytics workflows, or ML supporting infrastructure

 - Write Python and SQL code to process, transform, and validate data

 - Collaborate with data scientists, analysts, or software engineers to meet data or platform needs

 - Contribute to automated testing for data quality and pipeline reliability

 - Document your work and share progress with your team throughout the internship


QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum:

 - Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program at an accredited US university

 - Proficient in Python and SQL

Preferred:

 - Actively pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Data Science, or a closely related field, with intent to return to school after the internship

 - Coursework or project experience with data engineering, analytics, or machine learning

 - Familiarity with cloud data platforms such as Databricks, Snowflake, or Google BigQuery

 - Exposure to data transformation tools such as dbt, or infrastructure as code tools such as Terraform

 - Interest in applying data skills to vehicle, fleet, or manufacturing use cases


TOTAL REWARDS

We build the exceptional — and we believe the people doing that work should be rewarded accordingly. In addition to a competitive base salary, full-time positions may be is eligible to participate in our annual company performance bonus program. 



Payments are discretionary and not guaranteed; actual amounts depend on company results and the terms of the plan in effect, and require active employment at the time of payout. This role is also eligible for equity in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), subject to board approval and the terms of our equity incentive plans, including applicable vesting requirements. 



In addition to our compensation programs, we invest in our people with a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, wellbeing, and financial future for full-time employees — including health coverage, retirement savings, time off, and family planning programs. Offerings vary by country. Learn more about our global benefit programs https://rvtech.mybenefits.life/.



External candidates can apply for this role through the Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies careers site (https://rivianvw.tech/#careers). If you are a current employee, please apply through our internal job board https://app.ashbyhq.com/internal/job-board/b10a9912-eb45-4a84-9a34-84b2a459923a.

listings.title: Intern, Marketing Engineer
listings.desc:
Rockwell Automation is a global technology leader focused on helping the world’s manufacturers be more productive, sustainable, and agile. With more than 28,000 employees who make the world better every day, we know we have something special. Behind our customers - amazing companies that help feed the world, provide life-saving medicine on a global scale, and focus on clean water and green mobility - our people are energized problem solvers that take pride in how the work we do changes the world for the better. 
 We welcome all makers, forward thinkers, and problem solvers who are looking for a place to do their best work. And if that’s you we would love to have you join us! 
 Job Description 
 As a Marketing Engineering Intern, you will use your technical background to help shape how industrial power solutions are positioned, explained, and brought to market. You will work on real product marketing and launch initiatives, translating technical concepts into clear materials for customers, sales teams, and other partners. This is a strong fit if you are pursuing an engineering degree and want to explore work beyond a traditional design-engineering role. 
 You will join the Supply of Power business and collaborate with product management, engineering, sales, and regional marketing teams. You will work onsite in Milwaukee, WI at the start of the internship, with the opportunity to move to a hybrid schedule as you become established in the role.
 Your Responsibilities:
 Assist with product marketing strategies, product launches, and go-to-market materials for industrial power solutions. 
 Create and maintain marketing collateral, presentations, technical content, application stories, and white papers. 
 Develop clear customer value propositions and messaging that explains the value of Rockwell Automation solutions. 
 Conduct competitive product, market, customer-needs, and emerging-technology research. 
 Support field sales teams with product information, training, and customer-facing materials. 
 Develop customer success stories, case studies, and content for Automation Fair®, ROKLive, and other industry events. 
 Support digital marketing, demand generation, sales enablement, reputation-building, and customer awareness programs. 
 Collaborate across engineering, product management, sales, and regional marketing teams on multiple projects. 
 Help translate technical concepts into information that customers and non-technical audiences can understand. 
 Contribute to project-based work that may include customer or field exposure and hands-on technical assignments. 
 The Essentials - You Will Have:
 Pursuing a Bachelors or advanced degree from an accredited college or university 
 Legal authorization to work in the U.S. We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job opening. 
 The Preferred - You Might Also Have:
 Active enrollment in a Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Technical Marketing, or a related technical discipline. 
 A cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher. 
 Interest in industrial automation, electrical power, manufacturing, product management, or technical marketing. 
 Previous internship, co-op, academic project, technical writing, presentation, or leadership experience. 
 Experience developing or presenting technical content for technical and non-technical audiences. 
 Experience managing multiple projects or working across different functional teams. 
 Interest in combining engineering knowledge with customer, business, and marketing strategy. 
 What We Offer:
 Health Insurance including Medical
 401k
 Paid Holidays
 To learn more about our benefits package, please visit at www. raquickfind.com .
 At Rockwell Automation we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right person for this or other roles. 
 #LI-hybrid #LI-DNI
 For this role, the Hourly Salary Compensation is from $20 - $32. Our benefits for the US can be found here . Actual pay will be based on factors such as skills, knowledge, education, and experience.
 This position is part of a job family. Experience will be the determining factor for position level and compensation. 
 We are an Equal Opportunity Employer including disability and veterans. 
 If you are an individual with a disability and you need assistance or a reasonable accommodation during the application process, please contact our services team at +1 (844) 404-7247.

We are excited about the opportunity to work with you and glad you want to be part of a team of talented individuals who together are changing the way the world communicates.

Description 
 In this Summer/Fall 2027 Co-op (June/July - Dec 2027) opportunity at Skyworks, you will learn and participate in developing advanced, state-of-the-art RF front-end modules, working with seasoned engineering professionals and collaborating with subject matter experts within Skyworks. Not only will you get to know how things work in the industry, but you will also accumulate advanced technical knowledge and skills, valuable experience as well as explore full-time job opportunities at Skyworks. We are excited to have you as part of our team to help you start your professional growth and contribute to our success at Skyworks! 
 Responsibilities 
 In this role, your responsibilities will include but are not limited to the following:
 • Working with experienced engineers to design/develop RF/Microwave multi-chip modules
 • Evaluating and optimizing prototypes of RF/Microwave multi-chip modules
 • Running simulations using design tools such as Ansys HFSS, Keysight ADS, etc.
 • Participating and presenting in design reviews
 • Performing lab testing using standard RF test equipment
 • Troubleshooting and resolving design or technical issues• Collaborating with other engineers and technicians
 Required Experience and Skills 
 Currently enrolled in an Electrical Engineering (or related) MS or PhD program
• Commitment to work onsite for 6 month co-op
• Strong desire to learn, grow and make an impact
• Strong career interest in RF/microwave circuits and engineering
• Willing to share knowledge and collaborate with others
• Must have experience with Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook
• Experience with Ansys HFSS, Keysight ADS is highly preferred
• Hands-on experience in a lab using a network analyzer and other RF instruments is highly preferred
• Knowledge of transmission-line theory and circuit design is a plus

listings.title: Product Marketing Intern
listings.desc:
At TE, you will unleash your potential working with people from diverse backgrounds and industries to create a safer, sustainable and more connected world.
Works under the supervision of administrative division management to gain hands-on experience in various activities related to admin support, management, business support, etc.
 Segment, Business Unit or Corporate Group   
 This position will be part of the ​INDUSTRIAL & COMMERCIAL TRANSPORTATION (ICT) BUSINESS UNIT--From heavy-duty trucks to construction equipment, mining vehicles to fire trucks, as well as boats, motorcycles, and tractors, many leading manufacturers count on our reliable connectivity product​ 
 Work Location   
 The location for this position is ​REMOTE​
 At TE Connectivity, you’ll help bring our purpose to life by creating a safer, sustainable, productive and connected future. Your role as ​an Intern​ in the ​Industrial & Commercial Transportation​ Business Unit, will help us make the connections that move the world forward by: 
 Supporting the development and execution of strategic operations priorities 
 Driving projects that contribute to long term operations enablement of revenue growth  
 Developing plans to bring best-in-class operating practices into AD&M  
 Responsibilities  
 At TE Connectivity, you'll be part of a global collaborative culture where your ideas and contributions help enable the successful marketing and sales of innovative connectivity solutions. In this role, you will: 
 Optimize and maintain internal marketing and sales enablement platforms, ensuring teams can easily access the tools, content, and resources needed to support customer engagements 
 Organize and enhance content across platforms including SharePoint, Microsoft Teams, MediaFly, and Brandfolder to improve usability, consistency, and efficiency 
 Support the setup, organization, and ongoing management of sales and marketing assets, including product images, presentations, and technical collateral 
 Assist with the creation and coordination of product sample kits and sample packs to support customer evaluations, marketing campaigns, and sales activities 
 Collaborate with Product Management, Sales, and Marketing teams to gather requirements, improve processes, and support cross-functional initiatives 
 Identify opportunities to improve content organization, user experience, and operational efficiency across internal platforms 
 You’re the kind of person we are looking for if you:  
 Have earned a high school diploma or GED 
 Are currently enrolled in, or pursuing, a ​BA/BS or MA/MS​ Degree in ​Marketing​, ​Communications​ or ​Related Major​ from an accredited college or university—or have equivalent work experience (gap year students may also be considered). 
 Preferably have prior internship experience or have completed a major project 
 Demonstrate strong written and oral communication skills 
 Like to creatively solve problems using data and analytics 
 Are intellectually curious and a self-starter 
 Are authorized to work in the U.S. 
 I&D  
 TE Connectivity and its affiliates are equal employment opportunity employers. We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, marital status, pregnancy, protected veteran status, order of protection status, protected genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law. 
 Competencies 
 Values: Integrity, Accountability, Inclusion, Innovation, Teamwork
Compensation   
 •    Competitive base salary commensurate with experience: $20.91 – 45.04/hour  (subject to change dependent on physical location)
•    Posted salary ranges are made in good faith. TE Connectivity reserves the right to adjust ranges depending on the experience/qualification of the selected candidate as well as internal and external equity. 
 What TE Connectivity Internship Program offers 
TE has a robust internship program that provides our interns with an abundance of resources to feel included as part of our Team.  Every summer we coordinate various educational and networking events for our interns. The TE University Relations team will be hosting virtual meetups, information sessions, tours, skill building presentations, and topping it off with National Intern Day celebration activities.  
 A unique employee resource group we have is the Young Professionals Employee Resource Group (ERG). This group is committed to creating a highly engaged and empowered cross-functional network of young professionals by placing high value in Professional Development, Networking Opportunities and Community Involvement to drive the success of our interns.  
 In addition to the ERG, we also provide our interns with complete access to our internal library of self-lead courses. These courses include academies like leadership to help the interns develop their development in becoming future leaders at our organization. To help with their professional growth, we provide access to Mentors via our NAVIGATE platform. Mentors serve as a guide to navigate the organization and provide additional support in their career endeavors at the company. Our program provides a holistic experience for interns that targets professional development and personal growth.  
 Our internship program typically runs May thru August and gives students the opportunity to work on projects that contribute to the success of their team and build on their classroom experience. Throughout the 10–12-week program, interns will be provided with: 
 •            Onboarding & Orientation 
 •            Professional Development Workshops 
 •            Networking Opportunities 
 •            Operations Experience 
 •            Executive Exposure 
 Timeline 
TE Connectivity recruits on campus between September and March for New Grad (FT), Rotational, Internship and Co-op positions beginning in May. Once you have applied to a position, your resume and application will be reviewed. If you are selected to move to the next step in the application process, you will be contacted by a recruiter. Once you accept an offer, the onboarding process will begin in January for interns who have committed to offers in the fall semester and upon acceptance for interns who have committed to offers in the spring semester. 
 EOE, Including Disability/Vets 
 Important Notice Regarding Recruitment Fraud 
TE Connectivity has become aware of fraudulent recruitment activities being conducted by individuals or organizations falsely claiming to represent TE Connectivity. Please be advised that TE Connectivity never requests payment or fees from job applicants at any stage of the recruitment process. All legitimate job openings are posted exclusively on our official careers website at te.com/careers, and all email communications from our recruitment team will come only from actual email addresses ending in @te.com . If you receive any suspicious communications, we strongly advise you not to engage or provide any personal information, and to report the incident to your local authorities

 The Summer Learning & Development (L&D) Sales Intern – Instructional Designer will join Vertiv’s NA Sales Training team at the Westerville Academy for Summer 2027, gaining hands-on experience in the full training development lifecycle.
 Working alongside experienced Instructional Designers and Sales Trainers, the intern will help design, develop, and produce training materials across multiple delivery formats – including instructor-led training (ILT), virtual instructor-led training (vILT), eLearning modules, videos, job aids, and assessments – that enable NA Sales teams on Vertiv systems, products, and solutions.
 This role offers direct collaboration with subject matter experts, Sales Trainers, and Instructional Designers across the organization. The intern will contribute to meaningful, real-world projects while receiving mentorship and professional development exposure aligned to adult learning principles and Vertiv’s sales enablement strategy.
 RESPONSIBILITIES
 Content Development Support:
 · Develop learning materials across multiple formats (ILT, vILT, eLearning, videos, job aids, assessments) based on design plans from Instructional Designers
 · Build and format content using approved Vertiv templates and brand standards
 · Create and update presentation decks, facilitator guides, learner workbooks, and quick reference materials for NA Sales teams
 · Support integration of product updates and new solution information into existing training materials
 Sales Enablement Projects:
 · Support development of sales training programs enabling NA Sales teams on Vertiv systems, products, and solutions
 · Assist with new product launch training content development
 · Help create sales-focused learning paths, onboarding materials, and value selling content aligned with Vertiv's commercial strategy
 Collaboration & Professional Development:
 · Work with Instructional Designers and Sales Training Team to execute content development tasks with guidance
 · Collaborate with subject matter experts to gather and validate technical and sales content
 · Participate in review cycles and incorporate feedback into deliverables
 · Learn instructional design best practices and adult learning principles, including ADDIE methodology
 Administrative & Team Support:
 · Maintain organized documentation of project files and development assets
 · Support publishing content to the Learning Management System (Docebo)
 · Assist with course maintenance and version control
 QUALIFICATIONS
 · Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Marketing, Education, Instructional Design, Business, English, Technical Writing, or a related field.
 · Strong writing and editing skills with attention to detail and formatting consistency.
 · Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (PowerPoint, Word, Excel).
 · Experience with or demonstrated willingness to learn content creation tools such as Articulate Rise 360, Canva, Camtasia, and Vyond.
 · Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple tasks and competing deadlines.
 · Effective verbal and written communication skills; comfortable collaborating across teams.
 · Interest in learning and development, sales enablement, or corporate training.
 · Self-motivated with the ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
 · Passion for developing people and enabling business performance.
 EDUCATION AND CERTIFICATIONS
 · Associates degree in Instructional Design, Education, Communications, Technical Writing, or related work experience.
 · Certifications in Instructional Design or eLearning Development preferred.
 PHYSICAL & ENVIRONMENTAL DEMANDS
 · Standard office and classroom environment at the Vertiv Westerville Academy.
 TIME TRAVEL REQUIRED
 · None

listings.title: Summer 2027 Intern - Software Engineering
listings.desc:
This posting supports current and anticipated early-career hiring needs. Applying allows our recruiting team to consider you for opportunities that align with your qualifications, preferences, and availability. An immediate opening or interview is not guaranteed. 
 Where are these roles located?  You’ll have the opportunity to work with teams in:
 Colorado Springs, Colorado
 Irvine, California
 Longmont, Colorado
 Fremont, California
 Rochester, Minnesota
 San Jose, California
 System Tools Software Intern : 
 Build the software behind the technology. 
 As a System Tools Software Intern , you'll create the software that powers engineering teams and next-generation products. You'll design, develop, test, and improve tools that make systems faster, more reliable, and easier to build.
 In this role, you may:
 Design and develop system software, utilities, and engineering tools.
 Build or enhance operating systems, compilers, networking tools, databases, and Internet-based applications.
 Troubleshoot, debug, and optimize software performance.
 Collaborate with hardware and software engineers to ensure seamless integration.
 Help influence hardware design by developing software that works efficiently with new technologies.
 Applications Software Intern: 
 Create software that helps teams work smarter. 
 As an Applications Software Engineer , you'll develop applications that support employees, customers, and business operations. You'll design, build, test, and improve software used across enterprise systems.
 In this role, you may:
 Design, develop, and maintain commercial and internal software applications.
 Write clean, efficient, and maintainable code using modern programming languages.
 Test, debug, and improve application performance.
 Collaborate with teammates to build new features and solve technical problems.
 Create documentation that supports software deployment and ongoing maintenance.
 Data Analytics Intern : 
 Turn data into insights that drive better decisions. 
 As a Data Analytics Engineer , you'll build the tools and data systems that help teams understand performance, improve products, and solve business challenges. You'll work with large datasets to create meaningful insights that influence engineering and business decisions.
 In this role, you may:
 Design and develop data pipelines, databases, and data warehouses.
 Build software and automation tools for collecting, processing, and analyzing data.
 Create dashboards, reports, and visualizations that support decision-making.
 Partner with stakeholders to understand business needs and translate them into technical solutions.
 Analyze data to identify trends, improve processes, and solve complex problems.
 Firmware Engineering Intern : 
 Write the code that brings hardware to life. 
 As a Firmware Intern , you'll develop the low-level software that allows hardware devices to function. Working at the intersection of hardware and software, you'll help build reliable, high-performance embedded systems used in next-generation technology.
 In this role, you may:
 Design, develop, test, and debug embedded firmware.
 Write software using C, C++, assembly, and other low-level programming languages.
 Collaborate with hardware engineers to integrate software with electronic systems.
 Troubleshoot firmware and hardware interactions to improve performance and reliability.
 Support new product development from concept through production.
 This role is part of WD's early career development program. WD's early career development program is ideal for individuals at the early stages of their professional career.  Participants receive foundational training through structured onboarding, mentorship, and a curated development curriculum. The responsibilities of this role are typically aligned with candidates who have approximately 0–2+ years of relevant professional experience, though candidates of all experience levels are encouraged to apply.
 Systems Design & Integration Intern: 
 Bring complex systems together. 
 As a Systems Design & Integration Engineer , you'll help ensure hardware and software work together seamlessly. You'll collaborate across engineering teams to design, integrate, test, and optimize complete system solutions for next-generation products.
 In this role, you may:
 Define system requirements and technical specifications.
 Evaluate hardware and software compatibility.
 Coordinate the integration of multiple subsystems into complete products.
 Identify, troubleshoot, and resolve system-level issues.
 Recommend improvements that enhance system performance, reliability, and scalability.
 Required: 
 Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Systems Engineering, Data Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.
 Experience developing technical skills through coursework, internships, research, or personal projects using one or more programming languages such as C, C++, Python, Java, Go (Golang), SQL, JavaScript, or similar technologies .
 Familiarity with software development fundamentals, debugging, data structures, algorithms, operating systems, or other computer engineering concepts.
 Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills with a passion for learning new technologies.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively in a team environment.
 Proficiency with Microsoft Office and common software development tools (such as Git, Linux, or IDEs) is a plus.
 Interest in storage technologies, semiconductors, embedded systems, cloud computing, AI, data analytics, or other emerging technologies.
