listings.title: Firmware Engineer Intern
listings.location: Santa Clara, CA; Westlake Village, CA
listings.desc:
About Marvell 
 Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. 
 At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. 
 Your Team, Your Impact 
Marvell's firmware engineering teams span multiple cutting-edge domains, giving you the opportunity to work on technologies that power next-generation cloud, AI, storage, and networking solutions. Firmware engineers may contribute to secure, high-performance firmware for compute and custom ASIC platforms, embedded software for SSDs, or trusted firmware stacks for hardware security modules. Other teams focus on networking innovation, developing tools and firmware for dynamic services, or creating embedded solutions for high-speed PAM4 DSP chips and optical communication links. Across all groups, you’ll collaborate with hardware and software engineers to deliver robust, scalable solutions that enable Marvell’s leadership in data infrastructure. 
 What You Can Expect 
 As a Firmware Engineer Intern at Marvell, you could:
 Develop and maintain embedded firmware for advanced hardware platforms, including data center, AI devices, SSD controllers, DSP networking chips, and high-speed PAM4 DSPs.
 Design and implement device drivers and firmware features for communication protocols (SPI, I2C, I3C, UART, MDIO, PCIe, NVMe) and RTOS-based systems.
 Participate in full product lifecycle : concept, design, implementation, testing, validation, and release to customers.
 Create and enhance automation scripts (Python, shell, bash) for testing, failure analysis workflows, and infrastructure management.
 Develop provisioning software and trusted firmware stacks to enable advanced security features for SoCs, including cryptography and secure protocols (TLS/SSL, IPSec).
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Hardware, System, QA, Customer Solutions) for integration, debugging, and performance optimization.
 Design and execute unit, system, and integration tests , including regression planning and continuous integration (Jenkins).
 Support lab testing and data analysis , including tool development for debugging, proof-of-concept preparation, and customer documentation.
 Work on mission-critical features for top-tier cloud customers and gain exposure to DSP concepts (Equalizers, Filters) and networking fundamentals (Ethernet, TCP/IP, OSI model).
 Debug complex hardware/software issues , drive root cause analysis, and manage fixes through issue tracking systems (e.g., Jira).
 What We're Looking For 
 Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 and Summer 2028 
 Strong problem-solving, verbal, and written communication skills
 Proficiency in Python and/or C
 Comfortable working in Windows or Linux-based development environments
 Understanding of computer architecture, networking fundamentals (OSI model, TCP/IP), and/or embedded systems
 Knowledge or experience with any of the following technical skills:
 Git, GitHub, or Gerrit
 Linux, Makefiles, GDB, IDEs, and bash scripting
 ARM CPU, RISC-V, TrustZone, Caliptra, or Trusted Firmware
 RTOS architecture, device drivers, and communication protocols (SPI, I2C, I3C, UART, USB, PCIe, MDIO)
 Security protocols (IPSec, TLS/SSL, SPDM, digital certificates, cryptography)
 DSP concepts (Equalizers, Filters, ADC, DAC, FFE, DFE)
 Python/bash scripting, Jenkins CI, and software regression planning
 GUI development, lab automation, and customer SDKs
 Ethernet, SERDES, Switches, and Routers
 Unit testing, system integration, and debugging tools
 Expected Base Pay Range (USD) 
26 - 52, $ per hour. 
 The successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. The expected base pay range for this role may be modified based on market conditions.
 Additional Compensation and Benefit Elements   
Marvell is committed to providing exceptional, comprehensive benefits that support our employees at every stage - from internship to retirement and through life’s most important moments. Our offerings are built around four key pillars: financial well-being, family support, mental and physical health, and recognition. Highlights for our interns: medical, dental, and vision coverage, perks and discounts, robust mental health resources to prioritize emotional well-being, and paid holidays. Additional compensation may be available for intern PhD candidates. We look forward to sharing more with you during the interview process. 
 All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status. 
 Any applicant who requires a reasonable accommodation during the selection process should contact Marvell HR Helpdesk at TAOps@marvell.com . 
 Interview Integrity  
 To support fair and authentic hiring practices, candidates are not permitted to use AI tools (such as transcription apps, real-time answer generators like ChatGPT or Copilot, or automated note-taking bots) during interviews.
 These tools must not be used to record, assist with, or enhance responses in any way. Our interviews are designed to evaluate your individual experience, thought process, and communication skills in real time. Use of AI tools without prior instruction from the interviewer will result in disqualification from the hiring process.
 This position may require access to technology and/or software subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). As such, applicants must be eligible to access export-controlled information as defined under applicable law. Marvell may be required to obtain export licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce and/or the U.S. Department of State. Except for U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, or protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), all applicants may be subject to an export license review process prior to employment.

listings.title: Software Engineering - Intern, Graduate
listings.desc:
Job Details: 
 Job Description: 
 What if your next project helped power the future of technology? 
 At Intel, you'll do more than learn, you'll contribute. You'll work side-by-side with industry leaders, gain hands-on experience on meaningful projects, and help solve real-world challenges that affect billions of people worldwide. From advanced semiconductor manufacturing to AI-powered innovations, you'll play a role in technologies that redefine how the world works, learns, and connects.
 What makes Intel unique is the opportunity to see the entire technology lifecycle in action. Unlike many companies where hardware, software, and manufacturing operate separately, Intel brings them together, giving you exposure to everything from research and design to advanced semiconductor manufacturing and global deployment.
 Whether you're tackling engineering challenges, improving operations, analyzing data, advancing next-generation technologies, or supporting global customers, you'll build valuable skills while contributing to innovations that enable a more sustainable and connected future.
 Bring your curiosity, make an impact, and see where your ideas can take you at Intel. 
 What You'll Do 
 Build technologies that power the future of computing. As a Software Engineering Intern, you'll work on meaningful projects while building technical expertise that accelerates your professional growth.
 Design, develop, test, debug, and improve software that enables Intel products and platforms.
 Support code review, high-level design, scripting, automation, and validation activities.
 Contribute to open, secure software platforms and tools.
 Apply programming, data, and systems thinking to solve real engineering challenges.
 Collaborate with hardware, systems, product, and software teams.
 Develop technical depth, tackle complex challenges, and contribute from day one while learning alongside experienced Intel engineers and technical leaders.
 Where Your Career Could Take You 
 Potential opportunity areas include:
 AI Frameworks Engineer
 Cloud Software Development Engineer
 Firmware Development Engineer
 GPU Software Development Engineer
 Middleware Development Engineer
 Software Application Development Engineer
 Software Research Engineer/Scientist
 System Software Development Engineer
 System Software Validation Engineer
 Build technical expertise, explore new possibilities, and help shape what is next in computing and semiconductor technology.
 Qualifications: 
 Must possess the minimum qualifications below to be initially considered for this position. Experience may be gained through coursework, research, academic projects, internships, laboratory work, student organizations, leadership experiences, or other relevant experiences.
 Minimum Qualifications 
 Currently pursuing a Master’s degree or PhD in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, or a related STEM field.
 3+ months of experience gained through coursework, academic projects, research, internships, co-ops, student organizations, assistantships, or other relevant technical experiences.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 GPA of 3.0 or higher preferred.
 Experience or interest in design, architecture, programming, scripting, data analysis, automation, modeling, simulation, validation, or debugging.
 Hands-on coursework, research, projects, or internship experience related to the role family.
 Strong problem-solving, communication, collaboration, and ability to work in team-based environments.
 Location & Immigration Information 
 As you consider the opportunity to join Intel, relocation assistance may be available based on eligibility, current location, and the specifics of the role.
 Job location and modality of work will be communicated at time of offer. This position is not available in the state of Colorado. 
 This position is not eligible for employment-based visa/immigration sponsorship. 
 Intel sponsors individuals for employment-based visas for positions where we experience a shortage of U.S. workers. These skills shortage roles are typically STEM positions requiring a Master's or PhD degree, or a Bachelor's degree with at least three years of post-degree related job experience. This position does not qualify for Intel sponsorship because it is either a non-STEM position, or a STEM position that only requires a Bachelor's degree and less than three years' experience.
 For information on Intel's immigration sponsorship guidelines, please see: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/jobs/hiring.html

Job Details: 
 Job Description: 
 About the Internship 
 Are you interested in full-stack development, automation, and the tools that support GPU firmware engineering? Join Intel’s GPU Firmware Development Team to build practical software engineering and problem-solving skills through real projects.
 Our team develops firmware for multiple microcontrollers on GPU boards, along with the DevOps tools and continuous integration (CI) platforms that support daily development.  Develop Python tools and scripts to support firmware development, debugging, testing, and log analysis.
 Use and configure simulators and virtual platforms to establish environments for firmware development and testing.
 Firmware Testing and Development 
 Develop and maintain test cases and automated test scripts based on firmware requirements, and help analyze results and investigate issues.
 Collaborate with firmware engineers to improve test workflows, testing efficiency, and firmware quality.

 Proficiency in Python and C, with the ability to develop tools, scripts, test cases, or basic system functionality.
 Familiarity with Git and Linux development environments for day-to-day code management, development, and debugging.
 A basic understanding of GPU or embedded system architecture, including processors, memory, peripherals, and hardware–software interactions.

 Strong analytical thinking, a willingness to learn, and the ability to collaborate effectively.

 Experience with C++ development, embedded software, or microcontroller firmware projects.
 Understanding of real-time operating system (RTOS) concepts, such as task scheduling, synchronization, and inter-task communication.
 Experience using simulators or virtual platforms for software development and testing.
 Experience with automated testing, log analysis, or hardware–software debugging, including investigating and identifying the causes of issues.

listings.title: Software Engineer Intern - AI

To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before.  Strong problem-solving, analytical, and debugging skills.

listings.title: Engineering Software Developer, Intern
listings.desc: Overview Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do. Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers. In this role, you will evolve the Keysight Network Visibility (NVS) product line to support Service Provider features and newer technologies (e.g. 5G, 6G core network 3GPP standards). The NVS products allow our customers to tap, aggregate, filter, sample, and perform many other functions on network traffic for monitoring and analysis. Keysight’s network packet broker provides multiple applications: MobileStack – monitoring of customer traffic from a mobile user/session perspective (e.g. GTP, SIP/RTP) AppStack – monitoring of customer traffic from an application perspective (i.e. L4-L7) SecureStack – providing secure encryption/decryption for TLS1.3 (Active SSL) TradeVision – stock trading monitoring and analysis tool PacketStack – standard packet broker features such as aggregation, deduplication, masking, etc. NetStack – port tagging and VLAN stripping KVO – Keysight Vision Orchestrator – manages all the products and applications The focus of this job will be on mobility related functionality for the Service Providers, such as control plane/user plane correlation, meta data and orchestration. This includes virtualization of products and machine learning applications. Our MobileStack application tracks mobile users and sessions, sending the associated control and user plane data to specific network monitoring tools (i.e. probes) for analysis. In addition, the application load balances across probes and provides sampling, filtering, and VIP allow listing functionalities. This allows our customers to manage their probe bandwidth by looking at a subset of the overall network traffic, in addition to being able to troubleshoot specific quality of service issues. As network traffic continues to increase each year, our customers need solutions to monitor their network traffic more efficiently and cost effectively. Responsibilities Design, prototype and iterate on creative concepts to meet our user mobility requirements. Implement core network related protocol parsers and logic to provide filtering and sampling on mobile network parameters. Virtualize functions. Develop proof of concept applications for trialing with customers. Identifying methods for correlating user traffic to specific probes and patent methods. Participate in definition of new software product features and software. Rapidly solve problems and fix bugs. Participate in design and code reviews. Develop unit tests and perform feature/integration testing. Provide input and help resolve customer escalations for product issues. Use testing equipment (IxNetwork/IxLoad) or other popular traffic tools for traffic generation and protocol simulation. Collaborate closely with peers, including QA engineers and software developers in a distributed environment (US, Romania). Contribute new ideas and methods to continuously improve product quality and development efficiency. Qualifications Working towards completing a BS in computer science or related discipline. Coding in C++. Familiar with GIT. Strong debugging methodology. Familiarity with some type of protocol development helpful (wireless protocols, security protocols, Wireshark, etc.) is a plus. Exposure to telecom, service providers, communications a big plus. Extremely good English verbal communications skills and a desire for strong team collaboration. Experience with virtualization and microservice development (e.g. PODs, Kubernetes, Docker containers, Redis database) is a plus. Over and above, a commitment to your own quality work and a strong desire to help the entire team to succeed. Careers Privacy Statement***Keysight is an Equal Opportunity Employer.***

listings.title: Software Engineering Intern - Connected Systems (January - August 2027)
listings.desc:
ABOUT US

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.



The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.



Candidates should be available for a full-time commitment from January 11, 2027 to August 13, 2027.



This is a general application used to fill multiple internship openings across our Connected Systems teams. If selected, you will be matched to a specific team based on your background and interests during the interview process.

 - Connectivity Software Engineering Intern

 - Embedded Software Engineering Intern - Vehicle Access

 - Software Engineering Intern - Embedded Systems

 - Software Engineering Intern - Parallax Cloud Platform

 - Software Engineering Intern - Software Integration

 - Software Engineering Intern - Vehicle Connectivity




ROLE SUMMARY

At RV Tech, we develop next-gen vehicle features that include remote commands from mobile apps, OTA software updates, real time vehicle telemetry, and fleet management tools. All of which rely on cloud, connectivity, and integration software working together at scale. As a Connected Systems intern, you will work on the backend services, integration layers, or connectivity infrastructure that keep vehicles talking to the cloud reliably. This may involve high throughput data pipelines, distributed cloud services, or the software that validates features work end to end across the vehicle.

Specific project areas vary by team and may include:

 - Building and testing backend services that process vehicle telemetry and remote commands at fleet scale

 - Developing event driven, distributed systems using tools such as Kafka, Kinesis, or Redis

 - Contributing to cross domain systems integration and validation work, ensuring vehicle features function correctly end to end

 - Supporting connectivity infrastructure, including the messaging and communication layers linking vehicle, mobile app, and cloud

 - Working with cloud native infrastructure on AWS (EKS, Lambda, DynamoDB, IoT Core)


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design, develop, and test software components within an existing distributed or connectivity system

 - Write clean, maintainable code in Python, Go, C++, or Java depending on the team

 - Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and debugging sessions with your team

 - Contribute to test automation and validation for integration or connectivity features

 - Document your work and present progress to your team throughout the internship


QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum:

 - Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program at an accredited US university

 - Proficient in at least one of Python, Go, C++, or Java

Preferred:

 - Actively pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related field, with intent to return to school after the internship

 - Exposure to distributed systems, event driven architecture, or cloud platforms, AWS preferred

 - Familiarity with vehicle communication protocols such as CAN or MQTT, or IoT concepts

 - Coursework or project experience with backend development, systems integration, or test automation

In addition to our compensation programs, we invest in our people with a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, wellbeing, and financial future for full-time employees — including health coverage, retirement savings, time off, and family planning programs. Offerings vary by country. Learn more about our global benefit programs https://rvtech.mybenefits.life/.

As a Vehicle Controls intern, you will work on embedded software or controls algorithms for one of several vehicle domains, including propulsion and dynamics, energy storage and charging, thermal and HVAC systems, body controls, functional safety, or systems engineering and test automation supporting these domains.

Specific project areas vary by team and may include:

 - Developing controls software for thermal and HVAC systems, body controls, or lighting

 - Contributing to vehicle dynamics or propulsion controls algorithms

 - Supporting functional safety analysis and requirements for safety critical vehicle software

 - Building and running automated tests in Unit, Software in the Loop, or Hardware in the Loop environments

 - Working on systems engineering tasks such as requirements definition, architecture, or homologation


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design, implement, and test embedded software or controls algorithms for an assigned vehicle domain

 - Write production quality code in C or C++, with Python used for test tooling

 - Support test execution in SIL, HIL, or bench environments and help debug issues that arise

 - Coursework or project experience with embedded systems, control theory, or real time operating systems

 - Exposure to MATLAB and Simulink for controls modeling

 - Interest or coursework in functional safety concepts such as ISO 26262

listings.desc:
At TSMC Arizona, brilliance can ignite a world of innovation and launch a promising future. The world’s most brilliant innovators entrust us to transform their ideas into world-changing products that impact millions of lives. As long as you have the same passion to pursue excellence, you will find your fit here. 
 TSMC Arizona engineering departments are looking for engineering talents   to join our advanced technology fab, located in sunny Phoenix, Arizona. As a TSMC Intern , you will demonstrate a strong sense of reliability and enthusiasm and will possess an attitude that embodies our core values – Integrity, Commitment, Innovation and Customer Trust. 
 Job Roles: 
 Process Integration Engineer (PID) Intern 
 Focus on analyzing Inline and EOL (End-of-Line) electrical data to determine causes for issues, in collaboration with Integration, YED (Yield Excellence Department), and Process/Equipment engineers. 
 Yield Excellence Engineer (YED) Intern 
 Focus on defect inspection methodology to effectively deduce the root cause of critical issues by collaborating with respective stakeholders and innovate the current techniques to combat defect issues live on the production line. 
 Process Engineer (PE) Intern 
 Focus on delivering robust and efficient semiconductor manufacturing through data-driven analytics and systematic problem-solving. Optimize processes with experimental design, precision control, and statistical methods. Collaborate with suppliers to address technology gaps and focus on continuous improvement in stability, quality, yield, productivity, and safety.

 Equipment Engineer (EE) Intern 
 Focus on improving and maintaining tool performance in a cleanroom environment to ensure quality production. Key duties include troubleshooting alarms, installing and qualifying new tools, resolving critical equipment issues, and improving tool uptime. Additionally, the role involves enhancing hardware capabilities, implementing systems to prevent equipment failures, and managing vendor relationships while coordinating with facilities, vendors, and manufacturing teams.

 Advanced Material Handling System (AMHS) Engineer Intern 
 Focus on automated systems that ensure efficient, timely, and accurate wafer transfers. Projects may include improving Delivery Time Accuracy (DTA) or enhancing Stocker dispatching systems to optimize lot movement and cycle times.

 Quality Management Engineer (AQE) Intern 
 Support on TSMC's mission of world-class quality systems by collaborating with Taiwan's Central Quality team. Your role includes monitoring wafer fabrication processes, analyzing manufacturing parameters, applying statistical methods, and leveraging predictive analytics to optimize process control. You'll also contribute to product success during launches and technology ramps while ensuring compliance with global quality standards. 
 Product Engineering (PES) Intern 
 Focus on analyzing yield and process issues to support customer needs and drive improvements in semiconductor manufacturing. Your work will involve identifying process and quality "sweet spots" to optimize yield efficiency, performing detailed layout analyses to uncover root causes, and conducting electrical and physical failure analyses to pinpoint process-stage issues. 
 Mask Engineering Intern (EBO) 
 Be responsible for ensuring the performance, reliability, and efficiency of photomask tools within our advanced manufacturing operations. This role involves collaborating with tool owners to manage the installation and maintenance of photomask equipment, partnering with tool vendors to improve maintenance processes, and developing in-line monitoring systems to proactively identify and address potential issues.

 Focus on supporting the installation of manufacturing equipment and tools by conducting site assessments, preparing installation plans, and coordinating timelines with internal teams. You will work on projects such as surveying construction sites to identify optimization opportunities, developing improvement proposals, and presenting findings through reports or visual presentations. Demonstrate project management skills by identifying bottlenecks in the installation process and recommending solutions to streamline operations.

 Focus on supporting and promoting workplace safety and environmental sustainability efforts in advanced semiconductor facilities. Collaborate with departments to implement safety protocols, evaluate hazards (e.g., radiation, lasers, gases, chemicals), conduct risk assessments, and refine high-risk SOPs to ensure a safe and compliant work environment.

Work on projects like pattern recognition, machine learning, and web development while learning agile software development, implement Prometheus and Grafana monitoring services that were deployed to Kubernetes platform, implemented automated deployment pipelines utilizing Microsoft Azure DevOps and machine learning/statistics model or algorithms developed.

 Strong communication, computer, presentation, listening, working with others needed to contribute to the team and TSMC Arizona’s culture.

listings.title: Silicon Validation Intern, BS - Summer 2027
listings.desc:
About Marvell 
 Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. 
 At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. 
 Your Team, Your Impact 
The Rack Scale Switch Chip Validation team validates and delivers the high-performance switching silicon and system-level solutions used inside modern AI and cloud data center racks. As an intern, you will contribute to day-to-day engineering work such as running emulation and verification tests, debugging silicon and hardware issues, troubleshooting switch performance and efficiency, and writing scripts to automate workflows, all alongside experienced engineers. Your work will support the team's efforts to deliver reliable, high-bandwidth, low-latency switch products that are a key part of Marvell's data infrastructure portfolio. These products help customers scale AI workloads and enable the next generation of data center networking. 
 What You Can Expect 
 Support post-silicon validation of high-speed switch silicon under the guidance of senior engineers. 
 · Assist in developing, documenting, and executing test plans and test cases for switch chip validation. 
 · Support lab-based silicon bring-up and run unit tests on hardware and firmware functionality, including emulation and verification environments. 
 · Help collect and analyze high-speed signal and link data (such as eye diagrams, jitter, and BER) using lab test equipment. 
 · Assist in debugging silicon and hardware issues, and in troubleshooting switch performance and efficiency. 
 · Use diagnostics, software tools, oscilloscopes, and protocol analyzers to help isolate the root cause of failing tests. 
 · Write and maintain scripts (for example in Python) to automate test execution, data collection, and result reporting. 
 · Document test results, findings, and debug progress, and present them to the team. 
 What We're Looking For 
 · Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 – Summer 2028 
 · Foundational understanding of digital logic, computer architecture, and high-speed I/O concepts such as SerDes and PCIe or Ethernet protocols. 
 · Basic hands-on lab experience through coursework, research, or projects, such as hardware bring-up, testing, and debug. 
 · Familiarity with common lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, or BERTs. 
 · Programming or scripting experience in Python, Perl, or a similar language. 
 · Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with a willingness to learn. 
 Preferred/Plus: 
 · Coursework or project experience with PCIe, Ethernet, or other high-speed interfaces. 
 · Exposure to the physical and protocol layers of high-speed interfaces (for example PHY, PCS, MAC). 
 · Experience with emulation, simulation, or verification environments. 
 · Ability to read board schematics and layouts. 
 · Familiarity with signal integrity concepts such as eye diagrams, jitter, and BER. 
 Expected Base Pay Range (USD) 
28 - 56, $ per hour. 
 The successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. The expected base pay range for this role may be modified based on market conditions.
 Additional Compensation and Benefit Elements   
Marvell is committed to providing exceptional, comprehensive benefits that support our employees at every stage - from internship to retirement and through life’s most important moments. Our offerings are built around four key pillars: financial well-being, family support, mental and physical health, and recognition. Highlights for our interns: medical, dental, and vision coverage, perks and discounts, robust mental health resources to prioritize emotional well-being, and paid holidays. Additional compensation may be available for intern PhD candidates. We look forward to sharing more with you during the interview process. 
 All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status. 
 Any applicant who requires a reasonable accommodation during the selection process should contact Marvell HR Helpdesk at TAOps@marvell.com . 
 Interview Integrity  
 To support fair and authentic hiring practices, candidates are not permitted to use AI tools (such as transcription apps, real-time answer generators like ChatGPT or Copilot, or automated note-taking bots) during interviews.
 These tools must not be used to record, assist with, or enhance responses in any way. Our interviews are designed to evaluate your individual experience, thought process, and communication skills in real time. Use of AI tools without prior instruction from the interviewer will result in disqualification from the hiring process.
 This position may require access to technology and/or software subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). As such, applicants must be eligible to access export-controlled information as defined under applicable law. Marvell may be required to obtain export licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce and/or the U.S. Department of State. Except for U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, or protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), all applicants may be subject to an export license review process prior to employment.

ABOUT ADVANCED ENERGY                     
 Advanced Energy (Nasdaq: AEIS) is a global leader in the design and manufacturing of highly engineered, precision power conversion, measurement and control solutions for mission-critical applications and processes. AE’s power solutions enable customer innovation in complex applications for a wide range of industries including semiconductor equipment, industrial, manufacturing, telecommunications, data center computing and healthcare. Advanced Energy has devoted four decades to perfecting power for its global customers and is headquartered in Denver, Colorado. 
 POSITION SUMMARY:                                    
 Advanced Energy is currently seeking Electrical Design Engineering Interns and Co-Ops to support development activities across our North American design sites. Successful candidates will carry out their internships at Advanced Energy’s sites in Colorado, Minnesota, New York, or California. They will work with an experienced engineering team, closely collaborating on the development of high-performance, precision, efficient and cost-effective power conversion, metrology, or controls solutions. Both undergraduate and post-graduate candidates will be considered for fall and School-year internships. Candidates should be actively pursuing degree programs at one of the following institutions: University of Colorado, Colorado State University, University of Minnesota, University at Buffalo, Rochester Institute of Technology, California Polytechnic State University, San Jose State University, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, or Stanford University. 
 RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 Candidates may perform and support design activities related to any of the following: 
 Designing and implementing electrical circuits and printed circuit boards (PCBs) 
 Assembling and testing surface-mount PCBs 
 Conducting automated testing of electrical components using computer-controlled data collection 
 Analyzing collected data and visualizing results in Python 
 Developing mechanical systems and designing 3D models for project applications 
 Testing high-voltage circuits (up to tens of kilovolts) 
 Engaging in research on advanced technologies, including plasma applications 
 Additional tasks as needed to support project deliverables 
 WORK ENVIRONMENT: 
 Location: Milpitas, CA 
 Environment: In-office role in engineering, sales and manufacturing facility 
 Standard office environment; spends majority of the day moving throughout local buildings and helping users with PC problems at the user’s desk 
 Required to lift 40 lbs. repeatedly throughout the day. 
 Overtime may be required at times, including evening work, on-call weekends, and additional project hours.. 
 QUALIFICATIONS: 
 Majors in electrical engineering or related fields, with a strong academic record 
 Knowledge in electrical engineering fundamentals, with hands-on experience 
 Prior experience in power electronics or embedded systems (experience in plasma science is a plus) 
 Proficiency in physics, mathematics, and coding 
 Creativity, adaptability, and effective problem-solving skills 
 Eagerness to take on challenges and excel in a fast-paced, collaborative environment                             
 EDUCATION:                                                                                     
 Candidates working towards a bachelor’s degree with a minimum of 40 credits towards an Electrical Engineering (BSEE), or Computer Engineering (BSCE) degree, or equivalent

 GPA > 3.25 
 COMPENSATION:                 
 As required by multiple state pay transparency laws, Advanced Energy provides a reasonable range of compensation for each job posting. Actual compensation is influenced by an array of factors including, but not limited to, skill set, level of experience, and specific office location. The range of starting pay for this role is $25 to $35 per hour.   
 BENEFITS:

listings.desc:
What we are looking for 
 We are seeking innovators, collaborators, and problem solvers. Our interns do not shy away from a challenge, and are looking for a chance to create a real impact with our company. Avery Dennison’s Internship Program has a single business focus to cultivate future talent for our rapidly growing organization. With a concentrated blend of experiential on-the-job learning, a dynamic environment, access to business leaders, and an encouraging team of co-workers, peers, and supervisors, the Internship Program will provide you the opportunity to sharpen your skills and collaborate on a number of strategic projects. We’re seeking a Sales Intern to join our business in North America during the summer of 2027.
 What you will be doing 
 Customer & Business Exposure: Exposure to the Avery Dennison business and our customer base.   
 Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work cross-functionally to gain business insights and exposure to various aspects of the business.   
 Go-To-Market Strategy: Learn our go to market sales strategy and customer segmentation.   
 Skill Development & Efficiency: Develop key skills: Build skills in areas such as project management, relationship management, customer engagement, time management and negotiation, with key focuses around sales operational efficiencies and utilizing technology (including AI) to drive better and faster results.   
 Commercial Effectiveness: Potential project leader for enhancing commercial effectiveness or best practice.
 What sets us apart 
 Avery Dennison’s Summer Internship Program is unlike any other with its emphasis on networking, community and support. From Day 1, networking is encouraged, promoted and expected within the program. As you are on-boarded with other summer interns and Early Careers Program associates from various tracks, you quickly develop a community  of individuals all committed to make sure you have what it takes to succeed.

Some of our ERG’s are Black Employee Resource Group (BERG), Elevate(Women’s Leadership Development), NEO Chinese Association, Unite(LGBT+), Veteran Employee Resource Group (VERG) and Voz Latina.

 Avery Dennison has a long history of being an industry leader. Your history is important to us. It should include the following:
 Education

 Obtaining deep knowledge of RFID technology which can be a critical link for enabling the Internet of Things, Blockchain and Omni-Channel fulfillment

 Utilizing automated RFID test systems and RFID printer and reader systems to support testing, data collection, data organization, and reporting

listings.title: Chip Simulation Software Intern
listings.desc:
About Etched

Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.



The roles

Our chip simulation and tooling role will co-design, develop, and test simulations of our custom hardware and tools that engineers use to analyze those systems. You will be working at the cutting edge of hardware innovation, closely coordinating with both software and hardware teams across their whole development path. We are looking for Spring '27, and Summer '27 interns.



You may be a good fit if you have

 - Progress towards a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.

 - Proficiency in C/C++ or Rust

 - Strong fundamentals in data structures and algorithms

 - Strong understanding of low-level software engineering

 - Strong understanding of hardware/software co-design

 - Excellent communication and collaboration skills



Strong candidates may also have (Nice to have qualifications)

 - Experience with Linux internals, kernel development, or driver debugging

 - Experience with hardware diagnostics or interpreting hardware logs

 - Exposure to server virtualization or CI/CD pipelines

 - Experience with Rust or embedded development

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every qualification.



Program details

 - 12-week paid internship

 - Generous housing support for those relocating

 - Daily lunch and dinner in our office

 - Based at our office in San Jose, CA

 - Direct mentorship from industry leaders and world-class engineers

 - Opportunity to work on one of the most important problems of our time


For any questions, contact internships@etched.com



How we’re different

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson http://www.incompleteideas.net/IncIdeas/BitterLesson.html. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors.

 

We are a fully in-person team in San Jose (Santana Row), and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

listings.title: AI/ML Systems Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
listings.desc:
About GlobalFoundries   
 GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling AI at scale from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GF delivers differentiated, powerefficient and highperformance solutions for highgrowth markets. GF is a trusted and holistic technology partner for customers around the world. GF’s talented, global team remains focused every day on security, longevity, and sustainability. For more information, visit www.gf.com.
 Internship Program Overview:    
 Our Interns & Co-ops are our entry-level talent pipeline for GF across the globe. Our goal is to provide students with a meaningful work experience that will equip them with the skills to embark on a career in the fast-paced and growing semiconductor industry after graduation. As an intern at GF, you’ll experience one-on-one mentorship, work assignments that prioritize your growth and potential, professional development opportunities, and the chance to network with executives. 
 Summary of Role:   
 GlobalFoundries is seeking a curious and motivated AI/ML Systems Engineering Intern to characterize machine learning workloads and analyze how their compute and memory demands map to hardware resources. Working with experienced hardware and software engineers, the intern will build practical skills in performance experimentation, analytical modeling, and clear technical communication. 
 Essential Responsibilities include:   
 Run and interpret performance experiments for AI/ML workloads, including classical inference pipelines and modern model architectures, and document observations using reproducible analysis methods.  
 Build analytical models to estimate throughput, latency, utilization, operational intensity, and memory bandwidth requirements, and identify likely compute or memory bottlenecks.  
 Collaborate with hardware and software engineers to connect workload behavior with architectural and implementation decisions, including cache, memory subsystem, runtime, and compiler considerations.  
 Present findings through concise reports, visualizations, and technical discussions, and grow toward independent ownership of a defined workload characterization study during the internship. 
 Other Responsibilities:   
 Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs. 
 Required Qualifications:   
 Education – At least a sophomore at time of application and actively pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field through an accredited degree program during the time of internship.  
 Must have at least an overall 3.0 GPA and be in good academic standing.  
 Coursework or project experience applying linear algebra, probability, numerical analysis, or related mathematical methods to engineering or computing problems.  
 Working understanding of computer architecture concepts such as cache hierarchies, memory bandwidth, and CPU pipeline fundamentals.  
 Experience using Python and data analysis tools such as NumPy, pandas, matplotlib, or similar.  
 Language Fluency - English (Written & Verbal)  
 Travel - Up to 10%  
 Ability to work at least 40 hours per week during the internship. 
 Preferred Qualifications:    
 Prior related internship or co-op experience  
 Demonstrated prior leadership experience in the workplace, school projects, competitions, etc.  
 Strong interest in leveraging AI tools and emerging technologies to enhance productivity, streamline workflows, and support effective decision-making.  
 Project management skills, i.e., the ability to innovate and execute on solutions that matter; the ability to navigate ambiguity.  
 Strong written and verbal communication skills  
 Strong planning & organizational skills  
 Exposure to PyTorch or TensorFlow and concepts such as FLOP counting, operator-level profiling, or the roofline model.  
 Exposure to compilation, intermediate representations, or AI compiler toolchains such as MLIR, IREE, TVM, or similar.

listings.title: Intel Foundry/PCC Semiconductor Manufacturing Student Technician – ICE Program
listings.desc:
Job Details: 
 Job Description: 
 Why Intel Foundry?  
 Every technological breakthrough starts with a spark of curiosity and hands-on determination. At Intel Foundry, we design, develop, and manufacture the cutting-edge semiconductor chips that power the world—from AI-driven supercomputers and autonomous vehicles to global cloud networks and everyday smart devices.  
 As a Manufacturing Student Technician Intern, you won’t just read about semiconductor innovation, you will be inside one of the world’s most advanced cleanroom environments, operating multi-million-dollar toolsets and driving real-time wafer production. This 2-year part-time program is specifically designed for college students pursuing associate degrees, offering competitive pay, practical training, flexible scheduling around your classes, and an express ramp into high-tech manufacturing careers.  
 What You Will Gain  
 World-Class Cleanroom & Tool Experience: Develop hands-on operational and maintenance mastery over state-of-the-art semiconductor fabrication equipment.  
 Direct Technical Mentorship: Collaborate alongside seasoned process engineers, module technicians, and factory leaders invested in your growth and success.  
 Academic Flexibility & Total Rewards: Work compressed work-week shifts structured around your academic schedule, backed by industry-leading pay, performance bonuses, and benefits.  
 Key Responsibilities & Day-to-Day Impact  
 Drive Wafer Production & Operations: Oversee automated wafer fabrication and movement processes within the Oregon Fab network, maintaining strict adherence to quality benchmarks, output targets, and operational discipline.  
 Hands-On Maintenance & Troubleshooting: Diagnose equipment anomalies, conduct preventative maintenance (PM), and utilize precision hand tools and diagnostic fixtures to maximize equipment availability and yield.  
 Execute Technical Procedures: Interpret and execute instructions from comprehensive engineering drawings, schematics, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and technical specifications.  
 Cross-Functional Collaboration: Deliver crisp, concise shift pass-downs to incoming teams and partner closely with module teams to sustain continuous factory flow.  
 Uphold Safety & Cleanroom Standards: Serve as a safety champion by adhering strictly to fab safety protocols, chemical safety standards, and cleanroom contamination controls.  
 Work Schedule & Program Structure  
 Program Duration: 2-Year Cohort Internship Program.  
 Term-Time Hours: 20 to 32 hours per week during active school terms.  
 Break/Summer Hours: Up to 40 hours per week during academic breaks and summer sessions.  
 Compressed Workweek (CWW) Shifts (12-Hour Day Schedules):   
 Shift 5 (Day): Sunday through Tuesday (and alternating Wednesdays) | 7:30 AM – 8:00 PM  
 Shift 7 (Day): Thursday through Saturday (and alternating Wednesdays) | 7:30 AM – 8:00 PM  
 Additional schedule options available for AMHS Area 
 Shift8 (Day/Night) AMHS FH Sunday Through Tuesday (alternating Wednesday) | 12:00 PM – 00:00 AM   
 Shift8 (Day/Night) AMHS BH Thursday Through Saturday (alternating Wednesday) | 12:00 PM – 00:00 AM     
 This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship. 
 Qualifications: 
 You must possess the below minimum qualifications to be initially considered for this position. Relevant experience can be obtained through schoolwork, classes and project work, certifications, apprenticeships, internships, military training, and/or work experience.
 Minimum Requirements: 
 Active Student Status: Currently enrolled in good standing at a locally accredited community college, trade school, or university pursuing an Associate’s degree in Microelectronics, Automation STEM, or applicable technical trade.  
 Applicable fields include Microelectronics, Robotics, Electrical/Electronic Engineering Tech, Mechanical Technology, Automotive/Diesel Systems, Aviation Maintenance, HVAC, Machining, Life Safety Systems, Industrial Automation, Welding, and Precision Manufacturing.  
 Shift Availability: Ability to commit to at least 20 hours per week aligned with 12-hour compressed work-week factory shifts.  
 Preferred Qualifications  
 Sustained strong academic performance during rigorous first-term electrical and mechanical engineering coursework.  
 Demonstrated mechanical or electrical aptitude gained through hands-on projects, auto repair, robotics clubs, maker spaces, soldering, welding, vocational programs, or military technical experience.  
 Strong diagnostic, problem-solving, and logical reasoning skills with a commitment to continuous learning in a high-tech cleanroom environment.  
 Cleanroom Environment & Physical Expectations  
 Spend substantial shift time (>90% less break time) inside a high-tech cleanroom environment wearing full cleanroom attire (bunny suit, hood, booties, safety glasses, and nitrile gloves).  
 Ability to stand, walk, bend, reach, and lift to 45 lbs. across a 12-hour manufacturing shift.  
 Comfort utilizing precision tools, mechanical fixtures, and safety-rated equipment.  
 Compensation, Benefits & Growth  
 Intel offers a robust total compensation package, including competitive hourly rates, shift differential premiums, annual performance bonuses, stock opportunities, employee discounts, and comprehensive medical, wellness, and retirement benefits.  
 For more details on Intel benefits, visit: Intel Jobs & Benefits   
 Ready to build what’s next? Apply today and launch your semiconductor career with Intel Foundry!

listings.title: FPGA Design Intern
listings.desc: Overview Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do. Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers. Responsibilities Wireline Network Test is seeking an FPGA intern to support development of our wireline Ethernet test products. You’ll work with advanced technologies and standards, including FPGA logic operating at 600+ MHz and line speeds exceeding 1600Gbps. Join a highly talented and motivated team of hardware and software engineers developing a state-of-the-art wireline Ethernet test system. Leveraging the latest generation of FPGAs and multi-core CPUs, our test instruments are designed to stay ahead of mainstream solutions—enabling validation of equipment and networks before deployment. Driven by the growing bandwidth demands of hyperscale data centers and carrier networks, our systems must support the highest speeds and newest technologies well before they reach the market. This is your opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge innovations, working with line rates up to 1600Gbps and beyond. listings.title: PCIe Design Verification Intern - Spring 2027
listings.desc:
Today, NVIDIA is tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in an inclusive, encouraging environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how we can make a lasting impact on the world.  
 We are seeking to hire a PCIe Design Verification Intern in a six month role, working within February 2027 - August 2027. 
 In this role you will work in an SV/UVM test-bench, verifying PCIe and CXL hardware functionality and performance. Responsibilities may include enablement of new features (coding and debug), coding of coverage or checkers, simulation performance measuring/analysis/improvement, or automation of engineering processes and tools.
 What you’ll be doing: 
 Develop directed or random diagnostics to validate the processor Instruction Set Architecture (ISA), reference models, C simulation models, RTL models, HW emulators and real hardware.
 Write and review validation test plans.
 Debug of diagnostics on various platforms
 Collaborate with a worldwide team of engineers on planning, development, and deployment.
 What we need to see: 
 Pursuing a BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or related degree.
 Exposure to computer architecture, ASIC design,   or verification methodology is required.
 Familiarity with   Object Oriented programing and/or SystemVerilog
 Previous scripting experience in Python or Perl.
 Ways to stand out from the crowd: 
 Passionate about solving problems
 You're experienced with directed and random functional testing including writing test plans
 Familiar with automation of build, test, and other engineering processes
 Experience with hardware simulation and waveform debug tools
 NVIDIA is widely considered one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We employ some of the most forward-thinking and talented people in the world. Are you passionate about joining our life work to amplify human imagination and intelligence? If you are creative, collaborative, and have a real passion for design methodology and automation, we want to hear from you!
Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay based on the position, your location, year in school, degree, and experience. The hourly rate for our interns is 20 USD - 71 USD. 
 You will also be eligible for Intern   benefits . ​ 
Applications for this job will be accepted at least until October 16, 2026. 
 This posting is for an existing vacancy.

As we highly value diversity in our current and future employees, we do not discriminate (including in our hiring and promotion practices) on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any other characteristic protected by law.

listings.title: AI Kernel Engineer Intern
listings.desc:
Quadric is redefining edge AI with the industry's first General Purpose Neural Processing Unit (GPNPU), enabling developers to run both neural network inference and conventional C++ code on a single programmable architecture. Our technology powers intelligent edge devices across automotive, industrial, robotics, and embedded systems.

Founded in 2016 and based in downtown Burlingame, California, Quadric is building the world's first supercomputer designed for the real-time needs of edge devices. Quadric aims to empower developers in every industry with superpowers to create tomorrow's technology, today. The company was co-founded by technologists from MIT and Carnegie Mellon, who were previously the technical co-founders of the Bitcoin computing company 21.


THE OPPORTUNITY

As a AI Kernel Engineer Intern , you will work closely with our senior AI Kernel Engineers to help enable a variety of AI/LLM models to run efficiently on the Quadric platform. This is a hands-on role where you will dive deep into hardware architecture and optimization techniques. You will gain invaluable experience developing, profiling, and optimizing kernel code, directly contributing to the performance of our AI inference stack.

Note: Our preference is for this internship to be based out of our Burlingame, California office. Candidates should be based in the Bay Area or able to relocate for the internship period and available to work on site.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Develop & Implement

 - Assist in developing AI/LLM kernels and operators on the Quadric platform for efficient inference.

Analyze & Profile

 - Help profile kernel performance across compute, data, and parallelism to identify micro-architecture and software bottlenecks.

Code Optimization

 - Work alongside senior engineers to optimize C/C++ code to maximize hardware utilization for different workloads.

Collaborate

 - Partner across related areas of the AI inference stack to support team priorities and business goals.

Toolchain Contribution

 - Contribute to improvements in the Quadric toolchain, compiler, and runtime.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Within your internship, you'll:

 - Build a working understanding of kernel development and optimization for a GPNPU-class architecture.

 - Contribute kernel or operator work that meaningfully improves AI inference performance.

 - Develop hands-on fluency with performance profiling and hardware-aware code optimization.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Required

 - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.

 - Strong proficiency in C/C++ and Python.

 - Solid foundational understanding of computer architecture and hardware-software interaction.

 - Demonstrated capability in problem-solving, debugging, and clear technical communication.

Preferred

 - Academic or project experience with model and kernel inference performance profiling.

 - Exposure to or experience with compute development frameworks such as CUDA, DSP, NEON, or Triton-lang.

 - Familiarity with assembly language.

 - Previous internship experience in a hardware-oriented software role or AI/ML optimization.
   
   


WHAT WE OFFER

The hourly salary range for this temporary position is $50-57/hr . This range reflects the full span of levels and geographies at which Quadric hires for this role. The actual hourly salary offered will depend on a number of factors, including the specific level of the role, years and depth of relevant experience, technical skills and competencies.

Quadric interns receive hands-on experience working alongside industry experts in AI and semiconductor technology, with access to mentorship and meaningful project ownership from day one along with following

 

 - Catered lunch each day in our office

 - Downtown Burlingame office location, close to shops, cafes, and local amenities

 - A work culture focused on innovative disruption

If this role resonates with you, we encourage you to apply even if your experience does not perfectly match every qualification. We value potential, curiosity, and a willingness to learn just as much as direct experience.

 


EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

Quadric is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, medical condition, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law




E-VERIFY AND RIGHT TO WORK NOTICES

Quadric participates in the E-Verify program to confirm employment eligibility for U.S.-based roles. As part of this process, applicants may review the following notices, which explain your rights and our participation in E-Verify. These notices are provided in English and Spanish.

 - E-Verify Participation Notice (English | Spanish) https://www.e-verify.gov/sites/default/files/everify/posters/EVerifyParticipationPoster.pdf

 - Right to Work Notice (English | Spanish) https://www.e-verify.gov/sites/default/files/everify/posters/IER_RightToWorkPoster%20Eng_Es.pdf

No action is required from candidates during the application process. These notices are provided for informational purposes only.

 


PRIVACY

By submitting an application, you acknowledge that Quadric will collect and process your personal information as part of the hiring process. Please review our Privacy Policy  https://quadric.ai/privacy-policyto understand how we handle your data

listings.desc:

Posting Start Date:

Job Description: 
 About our group: 
 You will work in the HAMR Media Recording Physics and Advanced Development group at the Seagate Recording Media Research Center in Fremont, CA. Our team develops state-of-the-art magnetic, optical, thermal and spin-stand characterization techniques to advance recording physics understanding and guide the design of HAMR magnetic recording media for continued growth in data storage capacity. We collaborate closely with sputtering, testing, metrology, equipment, and materials science teams, as well as colleagues across Seagate worldwide. Together, we develop next-generation storage technologies for cloud infrastructure and emerging applications. 
 About the role - you will: 
 The candidate will work in the Recording Physics and Advanced Development group at the Seagate Recording Media R&D Center to develop and improve magnetic characterization methods, spin-stand recording tests, and data analytics used to study the magnetic, electrical, and thermal properties of advanced media. The role also involves comparing simulation and recording results to better understand the physics of HAMR (Heat-Assisted Magnetic Recording) and future recording technologies such as ferroelectric media. 
 Responsibilities include: 
 Develop metrology capabilities for characterizing ferroelectric media using electrical and imaging techniques such as Piezoresponse Force Microscopy (PFM), P-E loop measurements, and Raman spectroscopy. 
 Develop characterization techniques for HAMR and next-generation ferroelectric recording media by leveraging existing test methods and creating novel measurement capabilities. 
 Apply data analytics and AI-based techniques to compare experimental measurements with modeling results and improve understanding of recording physics and media design. 
 Translate characterization insights into innovative designs that improve the magnetic, electrical, and thermal performance of HAMR and ferroelectric media. 
 Integrate hardware and software for testing and data acquisition systems used in recording demonstrations and evaluation of advanced media designs and architectures. 
 About you: 
 Programming  
 Data analysis 
 Excellent communication skills 
 Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a creative environment 
 Your experience includes: 
 Strong background in physics, particularly magnetism or ferroelectricity, with hands-on experience using high-field magnetic characterization tools (PPMS and MOKE), as well as electrical, optical, and thermal measurement systems.
 Familiarity with optics, ferroelectric materials, recording physics, and programming languages such as Python, LabVIEW, Visual Basic, C, or related languages is preferred. 
 Experience designing and integrating novel instrumentation. 
 Strong experience with electrical characterization and PFM imaging of ferroelectric materials. 
 Demonstrated ability to develop and integrate new metrology or testing tools for advanced characterization of magnetic or ferroelectric materials. 
 Strong background in Magnetism and data analysis 
 Ph.D. or M.S. in Physics, Applied Physics, Materials Science, Electrical Engineering, Applied Optics, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field preferred.  
 Location: 
 Our Gold LEED-certified Fremont product-design campus drives innovation, bringing together a diverse set of engineering, design, operations, support, and administrative teams.  The site is equipped with a state-of-the-art clean room and lab space. On-site social activities are popular, including our annual BBQ, ice cream social, and holiday events. Wellness programs, gaming rooms, and the on-site fitness center help round out and balance your Seagate work-life experience, along with opportunities to give back to our local community. 
 The estimated base wage range for this position is $41 - $48/hr. The individual base wage is based on work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Seagate offers comprehensive benefits to its eligible Interns, including, but not limited to, medical, dental, vision, and participation in the employee stock purchase plan.  Seagate also offers Interns 12 paid holidays and a minimum of 48 hours of paid sick leave.  The benefits for this position are based on a 24 to 40-hour-per-week schedule for a full calendar year and may differ depending on work location and tenure with the Company.

listings.title: RFIC Design Summer Intern
listings.desc:
If you are looking for a challenging and exciting career in the world of technology, then look no further. Skyworks is an innovator of high-performance analog semiconductors whose solutions are powering the wireless networking revolution. Through our broad technology expertise and one of the most extensive product portfolios in the industry, we are Connecting Everyone and Everything, All the Time.
 At Skyworks, you will find a fast-paced environment with a strong focus on global collaboration, minimal layers of management, and the freedom to make meaningful contributions in a setting that encourages creative thinking. We are excited about the opportunity to work with you and glad you want to be part of a team of talented individuals who together are changing the way the world communicates.
 Requisition ID: 78242
Description 
 Join the Skyworks San Jose Design Center in developing high-performance silicon RFIC solutions for next-generation mobile applications. This internship offers hands-on experience in silicon RFIC design while working closely with experienced engineers in a collaborative team environment.
 The intern will contribute to the development of RF front-end integrated circuits from initial concept through production. The work will focus on transistor-level circuit design, simulation, layout, and laboratory evaluation of high-performance RF front-end circuits. The intern will also document results and present technical work to colleagues and stakeholders.
 Located in Silicon Valley near major customers, the San Jose Design Center provides access to highly integrated semiconductor, module, and embedded RF circuit design, an in-house prototype assembly laboratory, and a world-class RF characterization laboratory. This is an excellent opportunity to strengthen technical skills, expand a professional network, and prepare for a career in RFIC design.
 Responsibilities 
 •  Work with a mentor and design team to combine silicon RFIC design with RF and microwave electromagnetic simulation for high-performance RF switches, low-noise amplifiers, and other RF front-end components.
 •  Participate in product development activities, including product definition, architecture, system analysis, transistor-level circuit design, layout or layout supervision, top-level simulation, laboratory debugging, and production test support.
 Required Experience and Skills 
 •  Currently enrolled in an Electrical Engineering (or related) BS or MS programs
 •  In-person Summer internship beginning May/June 2027 (3 months) at the San Jose site
 •  Familiarity with transistor-level design concepts for silicon RFIC and analog circuits.
 •  Understanding of RF active-circuit requirements and design concepts, including noise, linearity, bandwidth, and small-signal and large-signal behavior.
 •  Understanding of microwave and RF fundamentals, including S-parameters, Smith charts, matching networks, noise figure, and transmission lines.
 •  Experience using time-domain and frequency-domain circuit and electromagnetic simulation tools, such as Cadence Spectre and EMX, Keysight ADS and Momentum, or Ansys HFSS.
 Desired Experience and Skills 
 •  Experience with on-chip passive circuit design; chip tapeout experience is a strong plus.
 •  Experience with RF test equipment, including network analyzers, spectrum analyzers, DC power supplies, and RF probes.
The typical pay range for an Engineering intern across the U.S. is currently USD $29.00 - $49.00 per hour and for a Non-Engineering intern across the U.S. is currently USD $23.00 - $42.00 per hour. Starting pay will depend on level of education, the ultimate job duties and requirements, and work location. Skyworks has different pay ranges for different work locations in the U.S.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Skyworks strives to create an accessible workplace; if you need an accommodation due to a disability, please contact us at accommodations@skyworks.com.

Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver.  Excited about working on self-driving cars!

 Colorado Springs, Colorado

 Rochester, Minnesota
 San Jose, California
 ASIC Engineering 
 Design the silicon powering the future of data storage.
 As an ASIC Engineer, you’ll help create the custom chips that power next-generation hard disk drives (HDDs). Working alongside experienced engineers, you’ll contribute to digital design, verification, simulation, and optimization to deliver high-performance, energy-efficient products at global scale.
 What you’ll do
 Design and verify ASIC architectures and digital logic
 Build simulations and validate complex hardware designs
 Support the ASIC development lifecycle—from architecture through synthesis, place-and-route, and timing closure
 Optimize performance, power, and reliability
 Collaborate across hardware, firmware, and systems engineering teams
 Technologies you’ll use
ASIC Design • RTL • Verilog/SystemVerilog • Digital Logic • Verification • Simulation • Timing Analysis • Low-Power Design
 Why you’ll love this role
 Help build technology that stores the world’s data.
 Learn from experienced semiconductor engineers.
 Work on cutting-edge silicon development.
 Solve challenging engineering problems with cross-functional teams.
 Build highly transferable chip design skills.
 Hardware Development Engineering 
 Build the hardware behind the world’s data.
 As a Hardware Development Engineer, you’ll help develop the technologies that make modern data storage faster, more reliable, and higher capacity. You’ll design, prototype, validate, and improve hardware while solving real engineering challenges alongside multidisciplinary teams.
 What you’ll do
 Design and develop electronic hardware and magnetic recording systems
 Create validation strategies and automated test solutions
 Perform reliability, stress, and performance testing
 Analyze circuit boards, processors, sensors, and other hardware components
 Improve products from prototype through manufacturing
 Technologies you’ll use
Electronics • PCB Design • Signal Integrity • Hardware Validation • Reliability Engineering • Test Engineering • Data Analysis
 Why you’ll love this role
 Design products used around the world.
 Work with advanced recording technologies.
 Gain hands-on laboratory experience.
 Collaborate with experts across multiple engineering disciplines.
 See your designs move from concept to production.
 Firmware Engineering
 Bring hardware to life through software.
 As a Firmware Engineer, you’ll develop the embedded software that controls advanced storage devices. You’ll work at the intersection of hardware and software, building reliable, high-performance firmware that enables world-class products.
 What you’ll do
 Design, develop, and debug embedded firmware
 Write software in C, C++, Assembly, and other low-level languages
 Integrate firmware with analog and digital hardware
 Troubleshoot hardware-software interactions
 Improve system performance, functionality, and reliability
 Technologies you’ll use
Embedded Systems • C • C++ • Assembly • RTOS • Hardware Interfaces • Firmware Validation • Debugging
 Why you’ll love this role
 Build software that directly controls hardware.
 Solve complex engineering challenges.
 Work closely with both hardware and software engineers.
 Learn how products operate at the lowest level.
 Develop highly sought-after embedded systems skills.
 Systems Design & Integration Engineering 
 Connect hardware and software into complete products.
 As a Systems Design & Integration Engineer, you’ll bring together hardware, firmware, and software to create reliable, high-performing storage systems. You’ll solve integration challenges and ensure every subsystem works seamlessly together.
 What you’ll do
 Define system requirements and technical specifications
 Integrate hardware, firmware, and software components
 Coordinate subsystem development across engineering teams
 Troubleshoot complex system-level issues
 Improve product performance, compatibility, and reliability
 Technologies you’ll use
Systems Engineering • Integration • Validation • Root Cause Analysis • Product Development • Cross-Functional Engineering
 Why you’ll love this role
 Work across multiple engineering disciplines.
 Understand how complete products come together.
 Solve challenging integration problems.
 Gain broad technical exposure.
 Build systems-level engineering expertise.
 Mechanical Design Engineering 
 Engineer the mechanics behind breakthrough technology.
 As a Mechanical Design Engineer, you’ll design the precision mechanical systems that support advanced storage products. From concept through manufacturing, you’ll help create innovative, reliable, and manufacturable solutions.
 What you’ll do

 Develop prototypes and evaluate new concepts
 Perform engineering analysis and design validation
 Conduct testing to improve performance and reliability
 Partner with manufacturing teams to prepare products for production

CAD • Mechanical Design • Product Development • Prototype Testing • Design Validation • Manufacturing Engineering

 Design precision mechanical systems.
 Build and test prototypes.
 Collaborate across engineering teams.
 See your designs manufactured at scale.

 As an Equipment Engineer, you’ll optimize the advanced manufacturing equipment used to build world-class storage technology. You’ll improve equipment performance, increase reliability, and help solve complex production challenges.

 Improve equipment uptime, reliability, and process performance

 Solve real-world production challenges.

 Learn automation and industrial systems.
 Help build products used around the world.

Working at the intersection of hardware, firmware, and silicon, you’ll design, integrate, verify, and validate complex SoC solutions that deliver high performance, reliability, and efficiency.

 Collaborate with ASIC, firmware, hardware, and systems engineering teams

 Work across silicon, firmware, hardware, and systems engineering.
 Experience the complete chip development lifecycle.
 Solve complex semiconductor design challenges.
 Develop highly marketable SoC engineering skills.
