listings.title: Manufacturing Test Development Engineer Co-op
listings.desc:
JOB DESCRIPTION 
 Co-op Cycle:  January 1st-July 2nd
 Schedule:  Monday- Friday 8:00am to 4:30pm 
 Location:  Beverly, MA (Onsite)  
 *To support students commuting to our Beverly, MA facility, we offer a travel stipend. See the Commute section below. 
 Ready to turn what you’re learning in the classroom into real-world impact?   
 Axcelis is a global leader in ion implantation and semiconductor technology.  Our co‑ops don’t just observe—they contribute . For more than four decades, we’ve been driving innovation in semiconductor manufacturing technology, working with the world’s leading chipmakers to power everything from smartphones to electric vehicles. As a co‑op, you’ll  gain hands‑on experience , learn from industry experts, and make a real impact on projects that shape the future of technology.  
 We are searching for our next group of engineering co-ops for a 6-month assignment at our Beverly, MA, facility. Our co-op program is designed to  develop earlycareer talent  and build a strong pipeline of  future engineers . Students gain  hands-on exposure , work on  real projects , and make  meaningful contributions . Throughout the program, co-ops build  technical skills , strengthen  problem-solving abilities , and gain  real-world experience  that enhances both their academic learning and future career opportunities.- 
 About the Role  
 As a  Manufacturing Test Development Engineer Co-op , you will gain hands-on experience designing, developing, and supporting test equipment used in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to help ensure products meet quality, performance, and reliability standards. This role provides exposure to real-world engineering challenges, including the design, development, and validation of electrical and mechanical test solutions, fixture design, and hardware-level debugging of test systems. Through this experience, you will develop practical engineering skills, learn how testing integrates into large-scale manufacturing, and contribute directly to improving efficiency and product quality. 
 What You’ll Do  
 Design, develop, build, validate, and maintain electrical and mechanical manufacturing test solutions, including automated test equipment and custom test fixtures 
 Leverage manual, subtractive, and additive manufacturing tools and techniques to meet fixture design and performance requirements 
 Collaborate with teammates across engineering disciplines, relying on their diverse skill sets to accomplish shared project goals 
 Analyze test data to identify failure modes, root causes, and process variations 
 Perform hardware-level debugging of test systems, including instrumentation and interfaces 
 Collaborate with manufacturing, design, process, and quality engineering teams to meet fixture design requirements of all shareholders 
 Create and maintain detailed test documentation, procedures, and reports 
 Support continuous improvement initiatives to increase test coverage, throughput, and repeatability 
 What We’re Looking For  
 Applicants must be candidates for a Bachelor of Science degree in any of the following fields: Electrical, Computer Engineering, Mechanical, Manufacturing Engineering or similar programs. 
 Familiarity with modeling software such as SolidWorks/Creo or AutoCAD 
 Familiarity with schematic and PCB design tools such as Altium, KiCad, QElectroTech 
 Familiarity with fabrication tools such as calipers, hand tools, 3d printing, etc. 
 Familiarity with measurement tools and equipment such as DMM’s, Oscilloscopes, Data acquisition systems (DAQ), etc. 
 Experience with project management tools such as Gantt charts, Microsoft Project/Planner, etc. 
 Why Choose Axcelis for Your Co-op?  
   Meaningful Work  – Work on real projects that make a direct impact on our products, processes, and customers 
   Leadership That Knows Your Name  – Senior leaders are invested in our co-ops’ growth and regularly engage with students throughout their assignment.  
 Mentorship  – Co-ops are matched with an experienced mentor to help them navigate the company, build connections, and succeed in their role. 
 More Than a Co-op  – Our co-op program is a key pipeline for full-time early career roles, giving you a strong starting point after graduation. 
 Engaging Co-op Experience : Enjoy off-site co-op events, weekly co-op meetups, and company-hosted luncheons that help you learn, network, and feel part of the Axcelis team. 
 Commute Information:  
 To support students commuting to our facility, Axcelis provides a  $1,000 travel stipend , paid as a  lump-sum in the first paycheck . Our headquarters in  Beverly, MA , is located directly off  Route 128  and just  10 minutes from the Beverly Train Station  for those using public transportation. 
 EQUAL OPPORTUNITY STATEMENT 
It is the policy of Axcelis to provide equal opportunity in all areas of employment for all persons free from discrimination based on race, sex, religion, age, color, national origin, disability status, medical condition (including pregnancy), veteran status, sexual orientation, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law.  Axcelis will provide reasonable accommodation necessary to enable a disabled candidate or employee to perform the essential functions of the position, unless the accommodation would create an undue hardship for the Company.
 U.S. BASE SALARY RANGE 
$20.42 - $35.70 
 This base salary range reflects the typical compensation for this role across U.S. locations.
 Our salary ranges are determined by role and level; individual pay is determined based on
 multiple factors, including job-related skills, experience, relevant education or training, work
 location, and internal equity. The range provides the opportunity for growth and progression as
 you develop within the role.
 Base pay is one part of our U.S. total compensation package which includes eligibility in the
 Axcelis Team Incentive bonus plan, and comprehensive benefits package (for regular
 employees working 20+ hours a week).

listings.title: Software Engineering Co-Op - Spring 2027
listings.desc:
We are seeking a motivated and talented Embedded AI Software Engineering Intern/Co-op to join our team for the summer. As an intern, you will work on cutting-edge embedded AI and computer vision applications for mobile machines, with a focus on optimizing AI models and real-time processing pipelines for deployment on embedded hardware.
 This role provides hands-on experience developing, deploying, profiling, and optimizing AI-powered vision systems on resource-constrained embedded platforms. You will work closely with our software engineering team to improve inference performance, reduce processing latency, and maximize hardware utilization while maintaining real-time system performance.
 Responsibilities 
 Collaborate with the software development team to develop and optimize embedded AI and computer vision applications for mobile machines.
 Deploy, benchmark, and optimize AI models for execution on embedded targets, including platforms equipped with hardware AI accelerators.
 Optimize real-time video processing and AI inference pipelines to improve throughput, reduce latency, and minimize CPU, GPU, and memory utilization.
 Profile and troubleshoot on-target performance bottlenecks involving image acquisition, preprocessing, inference, postprocessing, and video output.
 Explore AI model optimization techniques such as quantization, pruning, and hardware-specific acceleration to improve inference efficiency.
 Develop and optimize software components in C/C++ for embedded Linux and real-time operating systems.
 Integrate AI models with camera systems, sensor inputs, and embedded communication interfaces.
 Develop testing and benchmarking tools to evaluate model accuracy, execution time, memory consumption, and end-to-end pipeline performance.
 Document software architecture, optimization strategies, performance results, and implementation details.
 Participate in team meetings, code reviews, and technical discussions.
 Minimum Qualifications 
 Currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or another relevant technical field.
 Familiarity with C/C++ programming.
 Fundamental understanding of embedded systems and software development.
 Basic knowledge of artificial intelligence, machine learning, or computer vision concepts.
 Familiarity with Linux development environments.
 Strong analytical, debugging, and problem-solving skills.
 Excellent communication and collaboration abilities.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience deploying AI or computer vision models on embedded hardware.
 Familiarity with AI frameworks and deployment tools such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, TensorFlow Lite, or ONNX.
 Experience optimizing neural networks through quantization, model compression, or hardware-specific inference acceleration.
 Familiarity with embedded AI accelerators, GPUs, or NPUs, including platforms such as Texas Instruments TDA4.
 Experience with real-time video processing frameworks such as GStreamer, OpenCV, or similar technologies.
 Experience with embedded Linux, QNX, or other real-time operating systems.
 Familiarity with performance profiling tools and optimization techniques for CPU, GPU, memory, and system-level bottlenecks.
 Knowledge of image processing, object detection, or semantic segmentation models.
 Experience with embedded communication protocols such as CAN or Ethernet.
 Familiarity with cross-compilation, hardware debugging, and on-target software development.

listings.title: PCIe Design Verification Intern - Summer 2027
listings.desc:
Today, NVIDIA is tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in an inclusive, encouraging environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how we can make a lasting impact on the world.  
 We are seeking to hire a PCIe Design Verification Intern in a six month role, working from May 2027 - December 2027. 
 In this role you will work in an SV/UVM test-bench, verifying PCIe and CXL hardware functionality and performance. Responsibilities may include enablement of new features (coding and debug), coding of coverage or checkers, simulation performance measuring/analysis/improvement, or automation of engineering processes and tools.
 What you’ll be doing: 
 Develop directed or random diagnostics to validate the processor Instruction Set Architecture (ISA), reference models, C simulation models, RTL models, HW emulators and real hardware.
 Write and review validation test plans.
 Debug of diagnostics on various platforms
 Collaborate with a worldwide team of engineers on planning, development, and deployment.

 Pursuing a BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or related degree.
 Exposure to computer architecture, ASIC design,   or verification methodology is required.
 Familiarity with   Object Oriented programing and/or SystemVerilog
 Previous scripting experience in Python or Perl.
 Ways to stand out from the crowd: 
 Passionate about solving problems
 You're experienced with directed and random functional testing including writing test plans
 Familiar with automation of build, test, and other engineering processes
 Experience with hardware simulation and waveform debug tools
 NVIDIA is widely considered one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We employ some of the most forward-thinking and talented people in the world. Are you passionate about joining our life work to amplify human imagination and intelligence? listings.title: Test Engineering Intern
listings.desc:
The Test Engineering team designs, assembles and validates test solutions to be used in T&M Manufacturing facilities to test NI products at various stages of their assembly process.  We are seeking a Test Engineering intern who will work with our Test Engineers to assist with the design of these automated test systems. Come join our team! 
 In This Role, Your Responsibilities Will Be: 
 Designing or revising custom printed circuit boards to be used in a test fixture 
 Developing production test code for the next generation of NI products 
 Qualifying instruments for use in a Test application to be deployed to Manufacturing 
 Analyzing production test data to look for trends which indicate the health of the product and/or test solution  
 Who You Are:  
 You are passionate about learning about and working with test industry technologies. You are a quick learner with a strong work ethic and drive to succeed. You work effectively in a group environment, problem-solve, and diagnose technical issues and propose reasonable solutions.  
 For this Role, You Will Need: 
 Pursuing a Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering or Computer Science 
 Authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship now or in the future 
 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS THAT SET YOU APART:  
 High-level programming languages (e.g. LabVIEW, TestStand, Python) 
 Analog signal considerations 
 Sources of measurement error 
 Appropriate selection of instrumentation 
 Statistical analysis of data 
 Integration of hardware and software 
 Hands-on experience with electronic hardware 
 Experience with high frequency circuit design, RF and wireless communication is highly desirable 
 OUR OFFER TO YOU:  
 National Instruments (NI) is now the new Test & Measurement (T&M) business unit in Emerson's portfolio.  
 We recognize the importance of employee wellbeing and know that to do your best you must have flexible, competitive benefit plans to meet you and your family’s physical, mental, financial, and social needs. We provide a variety of medical insurance plans, with dental and vision coverage.  Employee Assistance Program, 401(k), tuition reimbursement, employee resource groups, recognition, and much more.  Our culture prioritizes work-life balance and offers flexible time off plans, including paid parental leave (maternal and paternal), vacation and holiday leave. 
 At Emerson, we are committed to fostering a culture where every employee is valued and respected for their unique experiences and perspectives.  We believe a diverse and inclusive work environment contributes to the rich exchange of ideas and diversity of thoughts, that inspire innovation and brings the best solutions to our customers. 
 The philosophy is fundamental to living our company’s values and our responsibility to leave the world in a better place. Learn more about our Culture & Values

 Software engineering experience in at least one compiled language and one scripting language 
 Understanding of modern software engineering practices 
 Experience deploying software systems into production environments

 Real, shippable RF front-end design experience at an industry leader.

 Coursework in electromagnetics, RF/microwave circuit design, and transmission line theory. 
 Understanding of S-parameters, impedance matching, resonators, and filter fundamentals.
 Familiarity with at least one EM simulation tool ( ANSYS HFSS, Keysight ADS/Momentum, Sonnet, EMX, or CST ).
 Basic scripting for automation and data analysis ( Python or MATLAB ).
 Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
 Desired Experience and Skills 
 Hands-on experience with HFSS or ADS Momentum for passive structure design.
 Knowledge of RF front-end architectures (PA, LNA, switch, filter/duplexer modules) and FEM integration.
 Exposure to module/package technologies (laminate, IPD, WLP, flip-chip) and their EM effects.
 Understanding of filter design (acoustic/BAW/SAW, LC, cavity) and matching network synthesis.
 Lab experience with VNA measurement, calibration, and de-embedding.

listings.title: Intern in Advanced Node Process Monitor Design
listings.desc:
At Cadence, we hire and develop leaders and innovators who want to make an impact on the world of technology. 
 Cadence is a pivotal leader in electronic design, building upon more than 30 years of computational software expertise. The company applies its underlying Intelligent System Design strategy to deliver software, hardware and IP that turn design concepts into reality.
 Cadence customers are the world’s most innovative companies, delivering extraordinary electronic products from chips to boards to systems for the most dynamic market applications including consumer, hyperscale computing, 5G communications, automotive, aerospace industrial and health.
 We are looking for an intern in Advanced Node Process Monitor Design 
 Title: Intern
 Location : Sophia-Antipolis, France
 Duration : 6 months
 From : early Q1 2027
 Internship Description 
 Are you curious about advanced technology nodes in microelectronics and eager to gain hands-on experience using them to tackle real engineering challenges? Do you enjoy solving problems and finding smarter ways to work? If so, we'd love to hear from you.
 At Cadence, we believe great candidates come from a variety of backgrounds and experiences. You do not need to be an expert in microelectronics or transistor technologies to apply. We are looking for motivated and curious individuals who are eager to learn and excited about exploring how today’s technologies and transistors can be used to address real engineering challenges.
 As semiconductor technology scales to ever-shrinking, advanced nodes, transistor variability during production (process variation) presents a critical challenge for integrated circuit design. Because of these variations, two integrated circuits originating from different wafers can exhibit significantly different behaviour.            
 Efficiently sensing process variations allows systems to be trimmed post-production, enabling an adaptive (rather than purely predictive) design approach, leading to tighter margins and superior performance at the system level. Embedded circuits capable of efficiently tracking process variations have therefore become increasingly critical in modern SoCs.
 In this internship, you will work with the Mixed-Signal IP R&D team to investigate available analog and digital circuit options to monitor process variations. After a thorough review of the state of the art, you will design and benchmark these circuits. Positioned at the intersection of circuit design and semiconductor physics, this project offers hands-on design experience in the mixed-signal domain, exposure to cutting-edge technology nodes, and the opportunity to directly contribute to the Cadence Mixed-Signal IP (MSIP) product roadmap.
 Internship Requirements
 Currently completing the final year of a master’s degree in electrical and/or electronic engineering.
 A genuine interest in circuit design and semiconductor technology.
 Some exposure to analog design EDA tools, such as Cadence Virtuoso, would be a plus.
 How to apply: please upload your resume onto www.cadence.com                     
 We’re doing work that matters. Help us solve what others can’t.

listings.title: Hardware Design Engineer Intern
listings.desc:
Do you want to design the physical hardware that measures and controls the world’s most critical industrial processes? Emerson’s Process Systems and Solutions business develops automation products that power the energy and manufacturing industries. We are seeking a Hardware Design Intern (Summer 2027) who is passionate about electrical and mechanical engineering and excited to gain hands-on experience in a collaborative, innovative environment based in either our Round Rock, TX or Austin, TX office.   
 You will join one of our hardware design teams that build the  controllers, I/O, and field devices  behind  DeltaV , our flagship distributed process control system used by leading chemical, life sciences, and energy companies around the world. Working alongside experienced engineers and mentors, you will take on a summer project drawn from our real backlog. Potential project opportunities include  PCB schematic capture, component placement, and board layout , FPGA design and verification, circuit simulation and analysis, or  mechanical design  work such as enclosures, thermal management, and manufacturability improvements. 
 No prior industrial automation experience is required.  If you enjoy designing and building things and want to see your work become hardware installed in plants around the world, we will teach you the rest. Many of our engineers joined us straight out of school from a general electrical or mechanical engineering background, and this internship is designed to be a great first exposure to professional product design. 
 In This Role, Your Responsibilities Will Include: 
 Partner with electrical and mechanical engineers and your mentor on a summer project that contributes to the hardware behind DeltaV controllers, I/O, and field devices. 
 Contribute to schematic capture, component placement, and PCB layout, from initial concept through a design ready to be built. 
 Support mechanical design work such as enclosures, mounting, and thermal management, and help evaluate designs for manufacturability. 
 Use simulation and analysis tools to evaluate circuit, thermal, or mechanical performance before hardware is built. 
 Work hands-on in the lab to bring up, measure, and troubleshoot prototype hardware using standard test equipment. 
 Participate in design reviews and testing, and learn how professional teams take a product from concept to release. 
 Take part in agile ceremonies such as sprint planning and retrospectives, along with Hackathons, Tech Talks, and Communities of Practice. 
 Document what you build so the team can maintain and extend your work after your internship ends, and present your results to the team at the end of the summer. 
 Who You Are: 
 You are curious about how products are designed and built, and you enjoy the challenge of turning requirements into a real, physical design. You like solving problems and can break them down into manageable pieces. You are methodical when tracking down an unexpected measurement and comfortable being hands-on in the lab. You ask questions when something is unfamiliar, communicate effectively, and thrive in a team-oriented environment where electrical, mechanical, and software engineers work side by side. You take pride in your work and are motivated by seeing what you design become hardware customers rely on every day. 
 For This Role, You Will Need: 
 Currently enrolled in an accredited college/university and returning to school following the internship. 
 Pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field. 
 Coursework or project experience with CAD tools, whether electrical (schematic capture and PCB layout) or mechanical (3D modeling). 
 Legal authorization to work in the United States. Sponsorship will not be provided for this position. 
 Preferred Qualifications that Set You Apart: 
 Junior or Senior standing. 
 Experience with schematic capture and PCB layout tools such as Altium Designer, Cadence OrCAD or Allegro, Mentor/Siemens Xpedition, or KiCad. 
 Experience with mechanical CAD tools such as SolidWorks, Creo, NX, or AutoCAD. 
 Familiarity with circuit simulation and analysis tools such as SPICE, or with thermal and structural simulation. 
 Exposure to digital and analog circuit design fundamentals, including power supply design and component selection. 
 Exposure to FPGA design and verification using an HDL such as VHDL or Verilog. 
 Understanding of signal integrity, power distribution, grounding, or thermal management considerations in board design. 
 Interest in design for manufacturability, enclosure design, or materials selection. 
 Awareness of agency and compliance requirements such as UL, EMC, hazardous location, or intrinsic safety. 
 Comfort with hands-on lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, and logic analyzers. 
 Coursework or project experience in a programming or scripting language such as Python, C, C++, or MATLAB. 
 Interest in applying AI/ML techniques to hardware design, simulation, or test problems. 
 Previous internship, class project, hackathon, or personal project experience in hardware design. 
 Our Culture & Commitment to You:​ 
 At Emerson, we prioritize a workplace where every employee is valued, respected, and empowered to grow. We foster an environment that encourages innovation, collaboration, and diverse perspectives because we know that great ideas come from great teams. Our commitment to ongoing career development and growing an inclusive culture ensures you have the support to thrive. Whether through mentorship, training, or leadership opportunities, we invest in your success so you can make a lasting impact. We believe diverse teams working together are key to driving growth and delivering business results. ​ 
 What You’ll Gain: 
 Real-world experience contributing work that ships as part of a product used in plants around the world. 
 Direct mentorship from experienced engineers and a close look at how professional teams design, build, test, and release products. 
 Practical, resume-ready skills in PCB design, mechanical design, and hands-on hardware bring-up and test.

listings.title: Software Development Co-op
listings.desc:
Software Development Co-Op 
Pay Range: $22.50/Hour
 Location: Onsite in Willmar, MN | No ability to work remote
Schedule: 40 hours/week
Timeframe: 6-9months  
 Who is Nova-Tech Engineering? 
Headquartered in Willmar, MN, Nova-Tech Engineering is a growing, dynamic company founded in 1992 that began as one person’s passion to benefit the agricultural industry.  Through innovative process automation technology, the company engineers and manufactures products that serve over 500 commercial poultry hatcheries in over 65 countries worldwide. 
Nova-Tech houses every aspect of its business on the MinnWest Technology Campus, including a manufacturing facility located just steps away from our engineering and drafting teams.  Walking from building to building, you can observe our whole process, from concept to final product.
 About our Co-Ops: 
Nova-Tech Engineering currently has full time, paid Co-Op opportunities located onsite in Willmar, MN. The Co-Op program is available to students entering their Junior or Senior year of college beginning January 2027 through August of 2027 or May 2027 through December 2027 for students pursuing Software Development degrees.  
 Learning Experience Objectives:  Build successful working relationships with members of a cross-functional team  
 Identify areas for professional development outside of core Software Development curriculum  
 Develop a general understanding of the various roles, processes, and procedures that support product development within a Software Development Group  
 With direction from the Product Owner and team, learn how to prioritize many competing tasks and project responsibilities to meet objectives on-time  
 Develop understanding of specific areas of skill and disciplines of interest within Software Development  
 Learn how to use an Agile Scrum framework to get work done in a collaborative team  
 Nova-Tech's Purpose Statement:  
We create revolutionary solutions that forever change industries and enhance quality of life. 
 Core Values at Nova-Tech Engineering:  Collaboration: We will combine diverse talents and work together to achieve our goals. 
 Agility: We will be flexible and adaptable to be successful.  
 Strengths: We will capitalize on the unique talents of each team member every day.  
 Innovation: We will inspire the application of imagination and science to create unique solutions to problems.  
 Excellence: We will excel by providing superior products, processes and services.  
 Servant Leadership: We will serve others to achieve our common purpose. 
 Strengths Based Culture:  
In 2005, we began training managers on the Gallup Strengths concept of discovering employees' natural talents and managing to those strengths in order to maximize engagement and productivity. A strengths-based approach is one that understands each employee brings a unique set of talents and drive to his or her job, and that if allowed to further develop and use those strengths, everyone wins.

 Interest in semiconductor manufacturing and global supplier collaboration. 
 What You'll Gain
 Hands-on experience with advanced semiconductor packaging technologies and manufacturing processes. 
 Exposure to cross-functional product development and supplier collaboration.

listings.title: Firmware Engineer Intern Fall Co-op
listings.desc:
Firmware Engineer Intern (Fall - Coop)
 Location: Vancouver, BC
 Job Description
 Astera Labs is a global leader in purpose-built connectivity solutions that unlock the full potential of cloud and AI infrastructure.
 Our Intelligent Connectivity Platform integrates PCIe, CXL and Ethernet semiconductor-based solutions based on a software-defined architecture that is both scalable and customizable.
 Inspired by trusted partnerships with hyperscalers and the data center ecosystem, we are an innovation leader of products that are flexible, interoperable, and reliable.
 We are headquartered in the heart of California’s Silicon Valley, with R&D centers and offices in Taiwan, China, Vancouver and Toronto, Canada, and Haifa, Israel.
 The mission of this role is to architect and develop firmware and microcontroller subsystems for Astera Labs’ SoC and systems products.
 Firmware is responsible for implementing the major differentiating features of Astera Labs’ products. As such, firmware is considered equally important to the hardware, and the firmware team is often customer-facing accordingly to ensure the needs of the customer are fully comprehended.
 Basic Qualifications
 Strong academic and technical background taking Computer Science, Electrical/Electronics/Software Engineering or equivalent.
 Completed one or more Co-op terms of firmware or embedded software development.
 Completed one or more courses in Real Time Operating Systems (RTOS) or detailed use of an RTOS during a prior coop term or project.
 Professional attitude with the ability to formulate theories and well thought out questions as part of helping debug/develop complex systems.
 Authorized to work in Canada and available for 4 or more months.
 Required Experience
 Proficiency in C (preferred) or C++, including development of firmware.
 Proficient in Python for scripting.
 Experience with developer workflows, SCM (preferably git), code reviews, CI.
 Experience developing firmware to execute in on-chip microcontrollers.
 Experience debugging firmware/hardware issues using JTAG, trace logs, or other lab tools.
 Preferred Experience
 Knowledge of tools like PyTest or GoogleTest is an asset.
 Knowledge of software build environments, CI/CD, gcc/make is an asset.
 Experience with lab hardware/firmware debug is an asset.
 Experience developing firmware for PCIe/CXL/Ethernet is an asset.
 Hourly compensation ranges between CAD $45/hour - CAD $55/hour.
 We know that creativity and innovation happen more often when teams include diverse ideas, backgrounds, and experiences, and we actively encourage everyone with relevant experience to apply, including people of color, LGBTQ+ and non-binary people, veterans, parents, and individuals with disabilities.

listings.title: Intern - RDA Application Engineer
listings.desc:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . 
 Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.
 Micron’s RAM (RDA and Metrology) group is responsible for advanced process control and precision measurement techniques that are critical to semiconductor manufacturing. The team focuses on defect detection, inline metrology, and signal analysis to ensure process stability and product quality. By using statistical methodologies, automation systems and AI enabled analytics, the RAM team drives ongoing improvement and supports the development of next-generation memory technologies. 
 We are seeking a highly motivated Process Integration Intern to join our RAM team in Boise, ID. This internship offers hands-on experience in semiconductor process integration, with a focus on in-fab measurement performance, RDA signal analysis, and process control optimization and the practical use of AI tool in manufacturing. You’ll be assigned a project designed to span the duration of your 3-month internship, with training provided to ensure safe and effective participation in cleanroom fabrication environments
 Responsibilities 
 Analyze defect and metrology data to identify process trends and anomalies.
 Use Micron's approved AI tools and macine learining methods to speed up data analysis, defect classification and reporting. 
 Support process control initiatives using SPC and DOE methodologies.
 Investigate deviations in measurement results and propose corrective actions.
 Collaborate with engineers to improve measurement accuracy, tool matching, and data integrity.
 Assist in tool health monitoring and calibration routines.
 Work with fab automation systems to troubleshoot data collection and integration issues.
 Identify repetitive tasks that can be automated or imroved with AI and document the time or quality gains.
 Take initiative to drive your assigned project to completion.
 Present findings in a verbal presentation near the end of the internship, including how AI was used and the impact it had on the project.
 Minimum Qualifications 
 Junior-level status in Electrical Engineering, Material Science, Physics, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related fields.
 Must be a current student and not graduating before September 2026.
 Passion for working in a fast-paced, high-tech environment.
 Ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize effectively.
 Strong technical, analytical, and communication skills.
 Proficiency in Microsoft Office and JMP.
 A mindset for continuous improvement and creative problem solving.
 Interest in applying AI tools responsibly to engineering problems, including checing AI generated results against the actual data. 
 Ability to recognize and escalate process anomalies with urgency.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Understanding of SPC (Statistical Process Control) and DOE (Design of Experiments).
 Experience with scripting, programming, or visualization tools (Python, Java, Tableau, Matlab).
 Strong data intuition and visualization skills.
 Familiarity with data collection systems, warehousing, and cleansing.
 Hands-on experience in data analytics and database querying.

listings.title: Signal Integrity Engineer Intern
listings.desc:
Signal Integrity Engineer Intern
 Location: San Jose, California, United States
 About the role
 Astera Labs is seeking a Signal Integrity Engineer Intern to join the Signal and Power Integrity (SI/PI) team. In this role, you will gain hands-on experience analyzing high-speed interconnects and supporting PCB- and system-level designs through simulation, measurement, and cross-functional engineering collaboration.
 You will work on a meaningful project with guidance from experienced engineers while building practical skills in signal-integrity analysis, lab validation, technical communication, and engineering judgment.
 What you will do
 Support pre-layout, layout, and post-layout signal-integrity analysis for high-speed PCB and system designs.
 Build or update simulation models and analyze critical interconnect behavior, including impedance, insertion loss, return loss, reflections, and crosstalk.
 Assist with S-parameter extraction, simulation, measurement, and interpretation for high-speed channels and differential signals.
 Support lab validation using equipment such as time-domain reflectometers, vector network analyzers, high-speed oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, and probing fixtures, with appropriate mentorship.
 Help plan and execute PCB/PCBA validation activities, prioritize critical items, and document results.
 Organize raw measurement data, screenshots, S-parameter files, and analysis results in project documentation.
 Collaborate with electrical, layout, validation, NPI, and other engineering partners to investigate issues and communicate findings.
 Contribute to technical reports, design reviews, and a final project presentation that explains the work, results, and impact.
 What you bring
 Enrollment in a bachelor’s, master’s, or Ph.D. program in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field.
 Academic, research, or project experience with one or more of the following: high-speed digital design, signal integrity, transmission lines, electromagnetics, PCB design, differential signaling, or S-parameters.
 A foundational understanding of frequency-domain or time-domain analysis and how interconnect design affects signal quality.
 Ability to learn simulation and measurement workflows, work carefully with technical data, and communicate conclusions clearly.
 Strong ownership, curiosity, practical judgment, and willingness to collaborate across functions.
 Preferred qualifications
 Familiarity with PCB or system-level SI/PI simulation, channel analysis, or lab measurement.
 Exposure to tools or workflows used for high-speed analysis, such as ADS, HFSS, CST, Keysight, Cadence, or equivalent platforms.
 Experience with Python, MATLAB, or another scripting language for data processing and engineering analysis.
 Familiarity with calibration, de-embedding, Touchstone/S-parameter files, eye diagrams, or BER analysis.
 Internship experience and compensation
 This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges from $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.
 Equal opportunity
 Astera Labs is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage anyone with relevant experience to apply.

You will support product bring-up and validation across lab hardware and software, help automate repeatable workflows, and collaborate with engineers across hardware, validation, firmware, and manufacturing.

listings.desc:

 Job Description 
 Applications are accepted until further notice.    
 Meet the Team 
 Looking for an internship that blends your communication skills with your need to dabble in technology? We’re looking for Technical Sales Interns who are interested in exploring a career as a Solutions Engineer, connecting people and business through technology.  
 What is a Sales Engineer exactly...   
 Corporations rely on technology to run their businesses. Splunk Products allow customers to investigate, monitor, analyze and act upon their data with one platform. The Solutions Engineer is the technical member of the Customer Account Team. They are the trusted advisor to both customers and the Sales Representative as the Splunk team collaborates to find the right solution for the business scenarios that are most important to the customer. Solutions Engineers tinker with the tech and translate it for a business ear. The ultimate goal, of course, is the success of the customer.  
 Your Impact 
 You know how to express yourself and you like to talk to people and learn what makes them tick. Cloud technology, analytics and data fascinates you! You’re passionate about learning, and thrive when things get exciting… and you tinker. You tinker with anything, be it mechanical or software. Helping people is satisfying to you, and the bigger the puzzle to get there, the better.  
 Splunk Solutions Engineer Interns will get the opportunity to become familiar with the Splunk Product line through observatory sessions with professional Solutions Engineers:  
 Partner with a Professional Solutions Engineer as they work.  
 Shadow customer calls and help out with presentation development, workshops and/or technical concept proof events as the account team moves the customers towards the close of sale.  
 Meet weekly with other SE Interns and mentors, and discuss what you’ve learned.  
 Learn how to present technical concepts to customers and how to discover their needs.  
 Collaborate with peers in developing a knowledge resource for subsequent intern cohorts.  
 Polish your evangelizing technique, talking about our products and services to customers (without being pushy!)  
 Minimum Qualifications 
 Actively pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Management Information Systems, Business Analytics, a related technical field or an established technical foundation. Applicants should also possess a strong record of academic achievement  
 Expected to continue enrollment in a degree or qualifying educational or workforce development program following completion of the internship.   
 Available to work 40 hours a week for 12 weeks. 
 Why Cisco? 
 At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.
 Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere. 
 We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

The DeltaV Product Marketing team is seeking a highly motivated Summer Intern to support strategic product management and product marketing initiatives for Emerson's DeltaV automation platform. The intern will work with Product Marketing, Strategy, Sales, and Technology teams on projects related to product direction, market positioning, commercialization, and customer value.

 In This Role, Your Responsibilities Will Be: 
 Support product vision and roadmap frameworks that connect investments to customer and business value.
 Evaluate emerging technologies, including AI trends, to help assess opportunities for future product development.
 Gain practical experience in roadmap planning, portfolio strategy, and cross-functional decision-making.
 Competitive Intelligence and Market Analysis
 Assess competitors, product offerings, market strategies, and potential areas of differentiation.
 Summarize market gaps and insights that can inform new product development and business cases.
 Product Adoption and Commercial Strategy
 Analyze product adoption, customer segments, commercialization approaches, and barriers to growth.
 Help define metrics and recommendations to improve market uptake and commercial performance.
 Business and Customer Insights
 Synthesize input from customers, sales, industry research, and internal stakeholders.
 Translate findings into clear recommendations, executive presentations, and business review materials.
 Develop executive communication and stakeholder collaboration skills.
 Who You Are: 
 You take on new opportunities and challenges with a sense of urgency, high energy, and enthusiasm. You consistently seek new and better ways to approach work, generating fresh ideas and experimenting with innovative solutions that add value. As an intern, you are eager to learn, proactive in contributing to team goals, and committed to continuous growth while making a meaningful impact.

 Pursuing a bachelor's degree in Chemical, Mechanical, or Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Business Administration or a related field.

 Interest in product management, product marketing, strategy, or technology commercialization.

 Rising Junior or Senior.

 Hubbell Incorporated

 Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. 
 At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. 
 Your Team, Your Impact 
The Board Product Engineering team's core mission is to develop and implement effective board manufacturing strategies that support the needs of Marvell's various Business Units (BUs).
Marvell is seeking a motivated Summer Intern – Board Product Engineering to support board-level product engineering activities during the summer internship program. This role provides hands-on exposure to new product introduction, board assembly, manufacturing test, supplier coordination, and product readiness activities for advanced hardware products. 
 What You Can Expect 
 The intern will work under the guidance of experienced engineers and cross-functional teams to help track engineering builds, collect and analyze manufacturing data, document issues, support readiness reviews, and contribute to continuous improvement activities. This summer internship is intended for students who want practical experience in hardware product engineering and manufacturing operations.
 Support board-level product engineering activities for prototype and pre-production hardware builds.
 Assist with tracking engineering build milestones, action items, risks, and readiness status.
 Help collect, organize, and summarize data from board assembly, inspection, manufacturing test, and validation activities.
 Support documentation of build issues, failure symptoms, corrective actions, and lessons learned.
 Work with hardware design, operations, test engineering, quality, reliability, and supply chain teams to support NPI execution.
 What You’ll Learn 
 How board-level hardware products move from prototype builds into manufacturing readiness.
 How engineering, operations, quality, reliability, and supply chain teams work together during new product introduction.
 How to organize build data, track issues, summarize technical findings, and communicate status to engineering teams.
 How manufacturing test, validation, and failure analysis activities support product readiness.
 How to contribute to engineering documentation, lessons learned, and continuous improvement efforts in a real product development environment
 What We're Looking For 
 Currently pursuing a BS degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
 Basic understanding of hardware products, printed circuit boards, electronics manufacturing, or product development processes.
 Coursework or project experience related to electronics, circuits, embedded systems, manufacturing, or mechanical design is preferred.
 Ability to organize technical information, summarize data, and communicate clearly.
 Comfortable working in a team environment and learning from engineers across multiple disciplines and regions.
 Familiarity with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, basic scripting, lab equipment, and CAD tools is a plus.
 Strong interest in hardware product engineering and manufacturing
 Curiosity and willingness to learn
 Attention to detail and good documentation habits
 Basic analytical and problem-solving skills
 Good written and verbal communication
 Ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams
 Self-motivated, organized, and able to follow through on assigned tasks

 Your Team, Your Impact 
As an Analog IC Design Engineer with Marvell, you’ll be a member of the Central Engineering business group. If you picture Marvell as a wheel, Central Engineering is the center hub providing IP to be used by all the other spokes on that wheel, including Automotive, Storage, Security, and Networking. You’ll be part of a small analog team making a big impact on this organization. Additionally, Marvell has the perfect size and scale for you to learn several aspects of engineering that will be new to you, but also have the time and freedom to dive deep into the details of your specialization on most projects. 
 What You Can Expect 
In this (hybrid/remote/in-office) role in LOCATION, you’ll build transistor level circuits from scratch or be given existing blocks to improve or port. Using a variety of CAD tools, but primarily Cadence, you will build or improve your circuit, simulate different performance metrics and measure other parameters. You’ll do circuit analysis and if your circuit looks good, you’ll send it to layout for physical design. Once it’s created, you get it back, run simulations and tests, and continue iterating until the circuit performs precisely as you need it to.
You’ll attend weekly meetings with your team to discuss your projects at a high level. If any issues arise, the team may take a more focused look at the problem to work out a solution. You’ll also attend meetings with senior designers and managers to review your work at a detailed level.  Smart Buildings Sales Internship  
  Here at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this through empowering customers by combining the real and digital worlds. Improving how we live, work, and move today and for the next generation! We know that the only way a business thrives is if our people are thriving. That’s why we always put our people first. Our global, diverse team would be happy to support you and challenge you to grow in new ways. Who knows where our shared journey will take you?    
 Who designs your future?  You do.  
 Are you looking for an internship where you can showcase your technical aptitude and passion for problem solving to ensure customers can work in a comfortable, safe, and energy-efficient environment? Does gaining hands-on experience, real-world skills and valuable knowledge while developing yourself professionally sound exciting to you? 
 Join our Siemens Smart Buildings Internship Program as a Smart Buildings Sales Intern in Summer 2027!   
 How long is the Smart Buildings Sales Internship and when can I start? 
 This internship is a 10-week program where you will rotate through various departments at your local branch office, focusing all on smart buildings and sustainable infrastructure.  Internship Program Start Dates: May 17, May 24, June 7 and June 14, 2027. 
 This is a hybrid sales internship supporting Building Automation, Fire & Life Safety and Security businesses, for both Solutions and Service Sales. 
 What is Building Automation? 
 Siemens Building Automation Systems is a building management system (BMS) that automatically manages and controls all systems within a building. These systems include lighting, heating, cooling, ventilation, fire detection and notification, CCTV, door and window controls, water and waste management. It consists of sensors, controllers, software and communication devices. Siemens offers building automation systems for all building types and sizes, and for every use. The system is designed to manage a wide range of building systems, such as HVAC, lighting, security, fire safety, and other critical building functions.
 Click HERE to learn more about Siemens’ Building Automation and Control Systems.
 What is the difference between Solutions & Service Sales? 
 The Solutions Sales Team is committed to supporting our new construction customers and will achieve booking and profit goals by developing and implementing plans to grow, develop, and manage contractor, consultant, developer, and end-user relationships; capitalize on sales opportunities within the territory; and effectively execute sophisticated deals independently within our established guidelines.
 The Service Sales Team is committed to supporting our Service Agreements business for commercial building automation controls, fire/life safety and security systems. The Service Sales Team supports our Operations Team whose focus is to perform service and maintenance in large commercial buildings such as hospitals, universities, and industrial facilities. 
 What will I do as a Smart Buildings Sales Intern? 
 Work alongside Sales Managers and Sales Executives within the local branch office.
 Assist the sales team with lead generation, prospecting, and account outreach.
 Support the preparation of sales presentations, proposals, and reports.
 Help manage CRM data by tracking leads and maintaining data accuracy.
 Shadow sales calls and meetings to learn effective sales techniques.
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams (operations, other business units, departments, etc.) to support customer engagement
 Analyze sales performance data and provide insights into driving growth.
 Participate in team meetings and contribute creative ideas for improving sales processes.
 Participate in sales related activities (learning how to prospect, go-to-market, build B2B relationships, on-the-job training and shadowing, etc.)
 ·        Rotate through our core business segments, which include Building Automation, Fire/Life Safety, Security and Energy/Sustainability Systems. 
  What will my responsibilities be as a Smart Buildings Sales Intern? 
 Position Siemens as an industry leader among service providers, leveraging Siemens world-class digital service delivery as a key differentiator. 
 Collaborate with operations and internal teams to deliver excellent customer outcomes. 
 Help prospect for new customers and engage with existing customers on new offerings. 
 Visit customer sites with both Solutions and Services Sales Teams. 
 Develop value-based proposals, estimates, specifications, and presentations. 
 Work with operations, finance, legal and other inside and outside resources to obtain the sale. 
 Attend job take-offs and turnover meetings. 
 Actively participate in sales department meetings, workshops, and seminars to stay knowledgeable on current market, business, and product trends. 
 The goal of this internship program is to develop future talent for the Siemens organization and help you identify where you may be interested in pursuing a career at Siemens post-graduation.  
 To apply for the Smart Buildings Sales Internship, candidates must meet the following requirements: 
 Education: Must be current enrollment as an undergraduate at an accredited 4-year U.S. college or university. 
 Majors:  Pursing a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Energy/Sustainability, Built Environment, Construction Management or Business Administration, Sales/Marketing with a strong technical engineering aptitude.   
 Preferred: Participation in a school sponsored sales engineering club/organization, pursuing a professional sales certificate or similar.
 Availability:   Ability to work 40-hours per week for the 10-week program (May - July or June - August).
 Relocation: No relocation assistance or housing stipend is provided.   Must be willing and able to work at the branch office location and surrounding local area.  
 Work Authorization:   Must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a continual and permanent basis without company or school sponsorship.  This program does not support students on a Visa such as F1, J1, M1 and H1B as well as OPT/CPT.
 Benefits: 
 The hourly pay range for this position is $24 - $28 per hour, based off of your projected graduation year.  The actual wage offered may be lower or higher depending on budget and candidate experience, knowledge, skills, qualifications, and premium geographic location.  Additionally, interns for Siemens are eligible to contribute into our 401K program.

About Marvell 
 Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. 
 At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. 
 Your Team, Your Impact 
The Operations team at Marvell is seeking a curious and driven Test Solutions Engineering (Post-Silicon Hardware Validation) Intern to join our team for a hands-on experience working
with cutting-edge silicon technologies. This internship offers a unique opportunity to work alongside experienced engineers in the validation of custom silicon and the development of test requirements for Marvell data center applications.

 Knowledge of basic statistics and data visualization techniques.
 Familiarity with scripting languages such as Python, Perl, or R in a Linux environment.
 Enthusiasm for problem-solving in a collaborative environment.

24 - 47, $ per hour.

listings.title: R&D Software Engineer (AI Developer Tooling), Intern
listings.desc: Overview Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Responsibilities Job Description Looking for a challenging position in software development? Come join Keysight for a summer internship in Colorado Springs and help us build the AI tooling our own engineers use to design and ship measurement software. You'll learn how to apply your engineering coursework and knowledge in software development to solve real-world problems. About the Job You will be part of an Agile software development team and will work on the design, implementation, and testing of internal tooling that helps Keysight R&D engineers develop software faster and better with AI. You will be assigned a self-contained project at the start of your internship, chosen from the team's active work so that it delivers something the team keeps using after you leave. It consists of sensors, controllers, software and communication devices. Siemens offers building automation systems for all building types and sizes, and for every use. listings.title: System Test Engineer  Intern
listings.desc:
Who You’ll Work With 
 Arista Networks is looking for world-class Software Test Engineers (aka System Test engineers) to help us in building the highest quality networking products for the AGNI team. 
 Arista Guardian for Network Identity (AGNI) is Arista’s network identity and access management solution. It provides secure authentication, authorization, and visibility for users, devices, and applications accessing the network. AGNI uses a cloud-native, microservices-based architecture and leverages ML/AI to simplify operations, support zero-trust security, and scale with modern enterprise networks. It integrates with existing identity sources and network infrastructure and is available as both a SaaS and on-premises solution.
 If you love networking, working on complex & scaled out network topologies makes you excited and if you like to challenge yourself to find the hard-to-find bugs and if troubleshooting & debugging network and system problems gives you a thrill, this role is tailor made for you.
 At Arista, you’ll bring your intelligence, creativity, and drive every day & work with our products exactly how they are going to be used by our end customers and while doing so, make sure that the products are going to work every time. You will engage with our products as end-users would, ensuring their consistent functionality and reliability. 
 Your job is to find the hard bugs, the ones not easily exposed by the developers’ automated unit and product level tests. You will NOT spend your time running manual regressions of mind numbing, 1000 page test plans, because Arista’s developers automate all the basic functional and integration tests. 
 Courtesy of our super collaborative work environment, you’ll spend your time embedded deeply with multiple engineering teams, working side by side with the developers, POC engineers, account teams, working together as one team and do all of it to help us to explore, find and fix software problems before they can reach the customers. We take quality seriously and we invite you to be a champion of software quality!!
 What You’ll Do 
 Work with the developers in your team in creating their plans for automated tests to complement the exploratory testing that you perform. 
 Participate in functional specification and software design reviews held by your team and provide customer centric input. 
 Work in a highly productive environment along with the best of the engineers on the Linux platform that cuts a typical development cycle by order of magnitude with a laser focus towards quality. 
 Use every means possible to find the bugs in the software and/or hardware being developed by your team. 
 Write test plans to validate Arista features and products. 
 Design test network topologies to validate functionality, performance, stability and scalability of features and products. 
 Execute test plans to verify all aspects of the product. Identify defects and validate resolution. 
 Work as an agile member of a combined development and test team, running in short cycles to develop functional software in quick iterations.
 BS CS/CE/EE plus 1+ years of experience. MS degree preferred 
 Experience in creating test methodologies and writing test plans or System Software skills. 
 Strong knowledge in the following areas: 802.1X, RADIUS, TACACS+, AAA, NAC, VLANs, IP Routing, TCP/IP, L2-L3 protocols. 
 Experience in configuring wired switches and/or wireless access points of different vendors for network access use-cases. 
 Familiarity with Identity Providers like Okta, Microsoft Active Directory, OneLogin are desirable. 
 Desirable to have experience in testing cloud-native SaaS applications ● Experience with working on other AAA or NAC products like ISE and ClearPass are desirable. 
 Good working knowledge of structured programming languages such as Python, Go, C, C++ etc. desirable 
 Strong communication skills.
 Compensation: 
 The intern base pay for this role is $80,000 to $85,000 / year.
 Arista offers different pay ranges based on work location, so that we can offer consistent and competitive pay appropriate to the market. The actual base pay offered will be based on a wide range of factors, including skills, qualifications, relevant experience, and work location.
 The pay range provided reflects base pay only.

 Coursework or project experience related to networking protocols and architectures.  
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively in a team environment.

 Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

 Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and teamwork skills.

 Understanding of memory architectures, memory subsystems, or DRAM technologies.
 Experience with circuit design and simulation tools through coursework, research, internships, or personal projects.
 Knowledge of statistics, data analysis, and engineering characterization methodologies.
 Experience with scripting, automation, or AI-enabled engineering tools to improve technical workflows.
 Demonstrated ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and solve complex technical problems.

Qorvo (Nasdaq: QRVO) supplies innovative semiconductor solutions that make a better world possible. We combine product and technology leadership, systems-level expertise and global manufacturing scale to quickly solve our customers' most complex technical challenges. Qorvo serves multiple high-growth segments of large global markets, including consumer electronics, smart home/IoT, automotive, EVs, battery-powered appliances, network infrastructure, healthcare and aerospace/defense. Visit www.qorvo.com to learn how our innovative team is helping connect, protect and power our planet. 
 Qorvo’s Internship Program is designed for college students currently enrolled in an accredited Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD program. Qorvo offers real work experience, exposure to upper management, and the opportunity to pursue full-time opportunities, as available. 
 Qorvo’s Internship Program offers: 
 Challenging, skill-building assignments
 Mentoring and coaching from industry experts
 Launch & Learns and other learning opportunities
 Collaborative team-based work environment
 Networking and social events
 Final presentation to business leaders
 Summary 
 As a Module Integrator Intern, you will work on the development of advanced RF front-end modules designed for 5G NR and 6G smartphone applications. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate individual high-performance hardware components into a single, optimized multi-chip module.
 Responsibilities may include   
 Contributing to the design of RF front-end modules (RF-FEM), including power amplifiers (PAs), silicon-on-insulator (SOI) dies, filter dies, and surface-mounted devices (SMDs). You will ensure that the modules meet target performance specifications while considering size, cost, footprint, and schedule.
 Building complex HFSS EM models of multi-functional RF front-end modules to extract the best possible performance, prevent unwanted coupling, and minimize shielding effects.
 Conducting full module simulations (FMS) across all functional states to identify compliance issues and proposing solutions to improve margins relative to specifications.
 Collaborating with team members to contribute design schematics, simulations, and real lab data.
 Qualifications 
 Currently pursuing a Master’s or PhD in Electrical Engineering
 Minimum GPA of 3.0
 Coursework and/or experience in RF and analog circuit design
 Strong understanding of fundamental electronics engineering concepts, including impedance matching using Smith charts, and RF/microwave parameters such as gain, loss, noise figure, and stability
 Hands-on experience with simulation and EDA tools, such as ADS, FEM, HFSS, Momentum, Cadence, EMX, and/or AWR
 Experience with passive RF structures such as filters, couplers, dividers, patch antennas, and/or active CMOS circuits tape-out, along with lab characterization using spectrum analyzers and network analyzers, is preferred
 Strong problem-solving skills.
 Self-starter with excellent communication skills for conveying complex technical information.
 Effective organizational skills for systematic planning and scheduling.
 Detail-oriented approach to ensure the design and delivery of high-yielding products.

Our portfolio of automation solutions help manufacturers to develop and deliver products quickly, efficiently and cost-effectively.  Our Purpose  
TERADYNE, where experience meets innovation and driving excellence in every connection. We are fueled by creativity and diversity of thought and in our workforce. Our employees are supported to innovate and learn something new every day. 
We cultivate a culture of inclusion for all employees that respects their individual strengths, views, and experiences. We believe that our differences enable us to be a better team – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better business results.
 Opportunity Overview 
 At  Teradyne , our Cooperative Education and Internship program is designed to deliver meaningful, fast paced and real-life work experiences that are relevant to your career and academic goals. Our program offers practical work experience in a business environment, with the opportunity to contribute and add value to the organization. 
 We are seeking an Electrical Engineering Intern to join our Innovation Lab group. In this role, you will work hands-on as a part of a team to design, simulate, prototype, and characterize RF and microwave hardware used in advanced instrumentation.
 You will be involved with the design, build, test, and refinement of next-generation mm-wave instrumentation. You will collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams, operate in an active lab environment, and present technical findings to practicing engineers.
 Responsibilities: 
 As an Electrical Engineering Intern, you will:
 Evaluate RF, microwave, and mm-wave hardware, including transmission lines, waveguide components, interconnects, antennas, and related passive structures.
 Develop electrical schematics, circuit models, PCB layouts, and prototype hardware using appropriate engineering tools.
 Conduct RF measurements using equipment such as Vector Network Analyzers, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, oscilloscopes, and power meters.
 Assemble, troubleshoot, characterize, RF and microwave prototypes.
 Develop test setups and laboratory automation programs for measurement, data collection, and analysis.
 Analyze measured and simulated data, document results, and present technical findings to engineering teams.
 Work with mechanical, manufacturing, and other electrical engineers to address packaging, interconnect, fabrication, and system-integration requirements.
 This position is 40 hours per week in North Reading (January-April). 
 All About You
 We seek individuals who share our passion and determination. Our commitment to customer success drives us to go the extra mile. If you’re ready to join us in this mission, take a closer look at the minimum criteria for the position.
 Pursuing a BS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electromechanical Engineering, or a related discipline.
 Experience with electrical laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, signal generators, or network analyzers.
 Strong hardware aptitude and comfort with hands-on assembly, measurement, troubleshooting, and prototyping.
 Ability to communicate effectively in both technical discussions and written summaries.
 Willingness to learn quickly, work independently, and contribute in a fast-paced engineering environment.
 Coursework or experience in RF, microwave engineering, electromagnetics, antennas, or high-frequency circuit design.
 Experience with schematic capture and PCB layout tools.
 Experience with laboratory automation and data analysis using Python, MATLAB, or similar tools.
 Familiarity with basic EM theory, s-parameters, soldering, cable assembly, PCB bring-up, and hardware troubleshooting are a plus.
 Experience with electromagnetic or RF simulation tools such as Ansys HFSS, CST Studio Suite, Keysight ADS, AWR Microwave Office, or similar tools is a plus.

 This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

The base hourly range for this role is $25.50-$47.00. This range is a good faith estimate, and the amount of base salary will correspond with experience and skill set. This range can also fluctuate depending on demand and location.

listings.title: Embedded Intern - Software Engineer
listings.desc:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.
 Software Engineering in the Hardware organization is where software meets the physical world. The Waymo Embedded Software Engineering team develops the critical, safety-critical software running at the edge of the Waymo driver, interfacing directly with steering, braking, propulsion, power distribution, and vehicle sensors. You will develop the abstractions and business logic to safely control and manage autonomous vehicles across different vehicle platforms and OEMs. Operating under stringent real-time, deterministic, and fail-operational constraints, the team builds high-reliability onboard firmware and off-vehicle simulation tooling, having a direct and material impact on Waymo's ability to scale safely to more vehicles and cities.
 Waymo interns partner with leaders in the industry on projects that create impact to the company. We believe learning is a two-way street: applying your knowledge while providing you with opportunities to expand your skill-set. Interns are an important part of our culture and our recruiting pipeline. Join us at Waymo for a fun and rewarding internship!
 You will: 
 Develop high-quality vertically-integrated C++ software systems (on-vehicle firmware and off-vehicle simulation/tooling) running at the edge of the Waymo driver.               
 Contribute directly to the bring-up, validation, and debugging of next-generation compute platforms, peripheral drivers, and hardware-software interfaces for new vehicle platforms.                                                                                                                  
 Write robust unit tests (such as gTest) and Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) simulation fixtures to validate edge-case handling, system robustness, and fault containment.                                                                                                                                           
 Analyze field data logs, vehicle telemetry, and simulation results to identify root causes and improve firmware performance. 
 Participate in cross-functional engineering workflows, design discussions, and code reviews alongside experienced embedded and systems engineers. 
 You have: 
 Enrolled in a BS or MS program in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical field.
 Strong programming foundation in C or C++, with a solid understanding of  data structures, pointers, and memory management.                          
 High curiosity, a continuous learning mindset, and the enthusiasm to explore unfamiliar hardware architectures, tools, and codebases.           
 Demonstrated problem-solving ability, debugging skills, and comfort navigating ambiguity when working with evolving platforms or prototypes.   
 Familiarity with Linux development environments, command-line tools, and version control systems (e.g., Git).
 We prefer: 
 Embedded Systems and Real-Time Programming: Hands-on experience developing software for microcontrollers (such as ARM Cortex-M or Cortex-R), bare-metal environments, or RTOS with resource-constrained execution.                                           
 Hardware Bring-Up and Lab Debugging: Practical experience with board bring-up, hardware-software integration, and lab instrumentation such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and multimeters.
 Testing and Quality: Experience with C++ unit testing frameworks like Google Test (gTest) and test-driven development methodologies.
 Open Source and Student Team Experience: Active involvement in collegiate engineering teams (such as Formula SAE, Formula Electric, Baja SAE, robotics clubs) or open-source projects demonstrating dedication to crafting high-quality modern C++ software.
 Scripting and Tooling: Proficiency in Python for test automation, telemetry data analysis, or build scripting.
 Note: This will be a hybrid onsite internship position. We will accept resumes on a rolling basis until the role is filled. To be in consideration for multiple roles, you will need to apply to each one individually - please apply to the top 3 roles you are interested in.
